findings.title: The echoed CURRENT_STATE.md snapshot is structurally one sv-commit stale, and the script prints it above a contradicting live git block in the same run
findings.evidence:
$ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py
...
## CURRENT STATE
# CDSFL Current State
Generated: 5 August 2026 14:08 BST (2026-08-05T14:08:53+01:00)
- **Last commit:** `686c515` TTS + plain-English record: the pipeline proven end to end
- **Remote:** diverged (ahead 97, behind 1)
- **Working tree:** DIRTY — uncommitted changes present
Uncommitted files:
- `M .claude/CLAUDE.md`
- `M bench/logs/simulated_bench_last.json`
- `M bench/tools/simulated_bench.py`
- `M experimental_notes/OUTSTANDING_QUEUE_to_BR2.md`
- `M experimental_notes/Simulated_Bench_First_Full_Run_2026-08-04.md`
- `M experimental_notes/adversarial_records/simulated_panel_alg02_findings_2026-08-04.json`
- `M resources/RECOVERY.md`
...
## GIT STATE
  Last commit: 624b39a sv: PROVENANCE CORRECTION -- ...
  Committed: 2026-08-05 14:08:53 +0100
  Remote: diverged (ahead 98, behind 1)
  Working tree: DIRTY
  Uncommitted:
    M experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md

Proof the two describe the same event, not two different states:
$ git show --name-only --format="commit %h" 624b39a | head -20
commit 624b39a
.claude/CLAUDE.md
bench/logs/simulated_bench_last.json
bench/tools/simulated_bench.py
docs/CURRENT_STATE.md
experimental_notes/OUTSTANDING_QUEUE_to_BR2.md
experimental_notes/Simulated_Bench_First_Full_Run_2026-08-04.md
experimental_notes/adversarial_records/simulated_panel_alg02_findings_2026-08-04.json
resources/ONBOARDING.md
resources/RECOVERY.md

The 7 files CURRENT_STATE.md lists as "uncommitted" are 7 of the 9 files committed IN 624b39a — the very commit that carries CURRENT_STATE.md itself. Reproduced forward:
$ python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py --dry-run
Collecting git state... done
=== CURRENT_STATE.md (dry run) ===
Generated: 5 August 2026 14:33 BST
- **Last commit:** `624b39a` sv: PROVENANCE CORRECTION -- ...
...
  Working tree: DIRTY

The snapshot that a future sv commit would carry names 624b39a — the commit BEFORE that sv commit.
findings.root_cause: Ordering in scripts/cdsfl_sv.py: `gs = git_state()` at line 724 captures git state, `generate_current_state(gs, ...)` at line 738 renders it into docs/CURRENT_STATE.md, and `_commit_and_push(...)` runs last at line 809. The hash of the commit that will contain the file does not exist when the file is written, so the Git block in CURRENT_STATE.md can never describe its own commit. This is INHERENT to a pre-commit snapshot — it is not a bug that can be fixed by better plumbing; the only mechanical alternative would be a post-commit `--amend`, which rewrites history. What IS fixable is that the file does not say so, and that scripts/cdsfl_recover.py:45 blind-echoes it as the first and most prominent section of the recovery output, 20+ lines above the live GIT STATE section that contradicts it.
findings.consequence: Every single sv produces a CURRENT_STATE.md whose Git block is wrong by exactly one commit, and the wrongness is invisible: it is well-formed, dated, and specific. A recovering agent that reads top-down — which is what "rebuild context from output" instructs — believes HEAD is 686c515, that seven named files are uncommitted work in progress, and that the branch is 97 ahead / 1 behind. All four beliefs are false. The dirty-file list is the most dangerous part: those files are already committed, so an agent trying to "finish the uncommitted work" would be re-doing landed work, and an agent deciding whether it is safe to switch branches would be deciding on a fabricated risk.
findings.proposed_fix: Two one-line changes, both making it honest rather than clever. (1) In scripts/cdsfl_sv.py generate_current_state (around line 375), change the heading from `## Git` to `## Git (snapshot taken BEFORE the sv commit — one commit behind by construction)` and add one line under it: `The commit carrying this file is not listed below; run scripts/cdsfl_recover.py for live state.` (2) In scripts/cdsfl_recover.py, move the `## GIT STATE` block (lines 60-71) ABOVE the `## CURRENT STATE` echo, and at line 44-45 compare the live `gs['last_hash']` against the hash parsed out of CURRENT_STATE.md; when they differ, print `!! docs/CURRENT_STATE.md snapshot is <n> commits stale (snapshot <hash>, HEAD <hash>) — its Git block is superseded by GIT STATE above` before echoing. Do not attempt to keep the snapshot current; label it.
findings.effort: Small — approximately 8 lines across two files, no behavioural risk.

findings.title: "(No experiment logs found)" is a false negative: latest_experiment() only ever looks at the single highest experiment number and never falls back, so two report-less exp53 control directories blackhole all 58 experiment archives
findings.evidence:
$ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py
## LATEST EXPERIMENT
  (No experiment logs found)

$ python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from cdsfl_utils import latest_experiment; print('latest_experiment() ->', latest_experiment())"
latest_experiment() -> None

But the logs directory is full:
$ ls bench/logs/ | wc -l
     315
$ python3 -c "...re.match(r'exp(\d+)', d.name)..."
matched dirs: 58
max_n = 53
dirs with max_n:
    exp53_control_zero_live_20260729T222431Z
    exp53_control_zero_live_20260801T005649Z

Neither exp53 dir carries the file the glob wants:
$ for d in bench/logs/exp53_control_zero_live_20260729T222431Z bench/logs/exp53_control_zero_live_20260801T005649Z; do ls "$d" | grep -i -E "report|summary|completion|final"; done
stage6_calibration_summary.json
stage6_calibration_summary.json
(no exp*_report.json in either)

A one-line descending fallback recovers a fully populated record immediately:
$ python3 -c "...for n in sorted({n for n,_ in exp}, reverse=True): ..."
FIRST HIT with descending fallback: exp 49
  dir      : exp49_engineering_exam_live_20260729T062320Z
  report   : exp49_engineering_exam_live_report.json
  experiment: exp49_engineering_exam_live
  target   : /Users/georgejackson/CDSFL_review_targets/exp49_engineering.md
  rounds   : 7 findings: 40
  converged_at: 6
findings.root_cause: scripts/cdsfl_utils.py:133 computes `max_n = max(n for n, _ in exp_dirs)` and line 135 filters `candidates` to `[d for n, d in exp_dirs if n == max_n]`. The `for exp_dir in candidates` loop at line 140 `continue`s when `exp_dir.glob("exp*_report.json")` is empty, and after the loop line 213 returns None unconditionally. There is no descent to n-1. The two exp53 negative-control runs (29 July and 1 August) archived checkpoints, per-round model JSON and a stage6 calibration summary but no `exp*_report.json`, so 53 is a dead maximum that shadows exp49, exp48, exp46, exp45, exp44 and every earlier archive. The comment at lines 122-124 shows the function was already patched once for a related exclusion bug ("so suffixed re-runs are not silently excluded"), which is the same class.
findings.consequence: Blast radius is wider than the recover script. scripts/cdsfl_sv.py calls the same function at line 732: `$ python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py --dry-run` printed `Reading experiment logs... none found` and then `No experiment data — skipping ONBOARDING.md experiment update`. So since the first exp53 archive landed on 29 July 2026, every sv has (a) written `No experiment logs found.` into the Latest Experiment section of docs/CURRENT_STATE.md and (b) silently skipped the ONBOARDING.md experiment-summary refresh. The `rs` output therefore states twice, in two different sections, that this project has run no experiments — in a repo holding 58 experiment directories and an arc of five consecutive convergences. Given the founder's own governing lesson, this is the expensive shape: an empty result that looks like a measurement.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the max-only selection at scripts/cdsfl_utils.py:133-138 with a descending scan over all distinct experiment numbers, keeping the existing mtime ordering within each number: `for n in sorted({n for n, _ in exp_dirs}, reverse=True):` then build `candidates` for that n and run the existing body; return on first success. Additionally, make the empty case loud rather than silent — have latest_experiment() return a marker such as `{'error': 'N experiment dirs scanned, none carried an exp*_report.json'}` so scripts/cdsfl_recover.py:97 can print `!! 58 experiment directories present, none parseable — investigate` instead of the currently indistinguishable "(No experiment logs found)", which today means "the newest two lacked a report file" and not "there are no logs".
findings.effort: Small — approximately 6 lines in one function, plus one print branch.

findings.title: "(No pending work section found)" is a dead marker: both the start and end strings the script searches for were deleted from RECOVERY.md in April 2026, and read_section returns the same empty string for "file missing" and "marker missing"
findings.evidence:
$ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py
## PENDING WORK
  (No pending work section found)

$ wc -c resources/RECOVERY.md
  193582 resources/RECOVERY.md

$ python3 -c "p=open('resources/RECOVERY.md',encoding='utf-8').read()
... for probe in ['NEXT STEPS:', 'NEXT STEPS', 'ARCHITECTURAL GAPS', 'IMMEDIATE NEXT STEPS']: print(repr(probe),'->',p.find(probe))"
'NEXT STEPS:' -> -1
'NEXT STEPS' -> 183683
'ARCHITECTURAL GAPS' -> -1
'IMMEDIATE NEXT STEPS' -> 183673

The near-miss is a single colon. The live text is `**IMMEDIATE NEXT STEPS (consult HIL before proceeding):**` at line 2289 — the colon sits after the parenthetical, so the literal `NEXT STEPS:` never matches.

When the markers died:
$ git log --format="%h %ci %s" -S "NEXT STEPS:" -- resources/RECOVERY.md | head -4
f5e73ab 2026-04-14 07:21:18 +0100 sv: Exp 39-0 gate complete, 10 bugs fixed, 793 tests green, morning report ready
$ git show f5e73ab:resources/RECOVERY.md | grep -c "NEXT STEPS:"
0
$ git show f5e73ab^:resources/RECOVERY.md | grep -c "NEXT STEPS:"
1
$ git log --format="%h %ci %s" -S "ARCHITECTURAL GAPS" -- resources/RECOVERY.md | head -4
f528314 2026-04-09 18:16:35 +0100 Enhance sv script: auto-update ONBOARDING.md and RECOVERY.md
$ git show f528314:resources/RECOVERY.md | grep -c "ARCHITECTURAL GAPS"
0
$ git show f528314^:resources/RECOVERY.md | grep -c "ARCHITECTURAL GAPS"

The end marker died 2026-04-09, one day after the script was written (file mtime Apr 8 01:18); the start marker died 2026-04-14. The section has therefore been empty for roughly 113 days.
findings.root_cause: scripts/cdsfl_recover.py:111 calls `read_section(recovery, "NEXT STEPS:", "\nARCHITECTURAL GAPS")`. read_section (scripts/cdsfl_utils.py:216-239) returns `""` on `OSError` (file unreadable/absent) at line 226 AND `""` on `start_idx == -1` (marker absent) at line 230. The two failures are indistinguishable to the caller, so line 116 prints one message covering both — and that message, "(No pending work section found)", is read by a human as a statement about the project ("there is no pending work") rather than about the parser ("my hard-coded marker no longer exists").
findings.consequence: The single most decision-relevant section of the recovery output has been blank since April while resources/RECOVERY.md grew to 193KB of live pending work, including a `## CORRECTION — 2026-08-05 14:05 BST` block written earlier today and a `## SESSION STATE — 2026-08-04 03:54 BST (READ THIS FIRST)` block carrying outstanding founder decisions. An agent following the spec literally — rebuild context from this output — concludes there is nothing pending and proceeds. Note also that the obvious replacement target is itself stale: the sv-managed block `<!-- SV:PENDING_START -->` (RECOVERY.md line 799) to `<!-- SV:PENDING_END -->` (line 2375) contains 125,435 characters whose newest entry is dated 2026-06-03, two months behind the hand-written SESSION STATE blocks above it.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not chase a marker. Two changes. (1) In scripts/cdsfl_recover.py replace lines 110-116 with a read of RECOVERY.md's own purpose-built short section: `read_section(recovery, "## Minimum Recovery", "\n## ")` — verified live, it returns 16 lines / 1474 chars and it already names the operational tracker as the first read — followed by printing the first 3 second-level headings found at the top of RECOVERY.md (today: the 2026-08-05 correction and the 2026-08-04 READ-THIS-FIRST session state) plus the line `Full pending work: resources/RECOVERY.md (193KB) — read it directly; this is a pointer, not a substitute.` (2) Make the failure loud: when read_section returns empty but the file exists, print `!! resources/RECOVERY.md exists (193582 bytes) but section marker '<marker>' is absent — the marker was removed in f5e73ab (2026-04-14); this section is NOT empty, the parser is broken` rather than "(No pending work section found)". Optionally give read_section a distinct sentinel for missing-file vs missing-marker so no caller can conflate them again.
findings.effort: Small — approximately 15 lines in cdsfl_recover.py, optionally 3 in cdsfl_utils.read_section.

findings.title: NOT ON THE SUSPECT LIST — the live GIT STATE block reports "Remote: diverged (ahead 98, behind 1)" when the checked-out branch is exactly in sync with its real upstream; the comparison is hard-coded against origin/main
findings.evidence:
$ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py
## GIT STATE
  Branch: exp39-experimental
  Remote: diverged (ahead 98, behind 1)

$ git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}
origin/exp39-experimental
$ echo "vs origin/main:            ahead $(git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD) behind $(git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main)"
vs origin/main:            ahead 98 behind 1
$ echo "vs origin/exp39-experimental: ahead $(git rev-list --count origin/exp39-experimental..HEAD) behind $(git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/exp39-experimental)"
vs origin/exp39-experimental: ahead 0 behind 0
$ git branch -r | head
  origin/HEAD -> origin/main
  origin/claude/assess-project-status-xJZqM
  origin/claude/debug-api-500-error-AFfcu
  origin/exp38-experimental
  origin/exp39-experimental
  origin/main

The branch's upstream exists, is tracked, and is fully synchronised. "diverged (ahead 98, behind 1)" is a measurement against a branch nobody is on.
findings.root_cause: scripts/cdsfl_utils.py:66-67 hard-code the comparison: `ahead = _run_git("rev-list", "--count", "origin/main..HEAD")` and `behind = _run_git("rev-list", "--count", "HEAD..origin/main")`. The branch's configured upstream (`@{u}`) is never consulted, even though `branch` is already read at line 52. On a long-running feature branch — which this project has used continuously since the exp38/exp39 branches were cut — being 98 commits ahead of main is the normal, expected, healthy state and carries no information about whether the work is pushed.
findings.consequence: This is the same shape as the defects the founder catalogued: a well-formed sentence that means the opposite of the truth. "diverged (ahead 98, behind 1)" reads as "you have 98 unpushed commits and are one commit behind the remote" — an alarm. The correct reading is "fully pushed, nothing to pull". A recovering agent acting on the alarm would reach for `git pull`, `git fetch && git rebase`, or `git push`, all on a false premise, and two of those are history-altering on a branch carrying 98 commits of borrowed-money work. Worse, the number is unresponsive to the thing it appears to measure: if origin/exp39-experimental were genuinely five commits behind HEAD, this display would still read "ahead 98, behind 1", so a real unpushed-work condition is masked. The same false figure is written into docs/CURRENT_STATE.md by scripts/cdsfl_sv.py:380 and thus into the committed record at every sv.
findings.proposed_fix: In scripts/cdsfl_utils.py git_state(), resolve the upstream first and compare against it: `upstream = _run_git("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "--symbolic-full-name", "@{u}")`; if it is non-empty use `f"{upstream}..HEAD"` and `f"HEAD..{upstream}"`, and label the output with the ref actually used, e.g. `Remote: up to date (vs origin/exp39-experimental)`. If no upstream is configured, print `Remote: no upstream configured for <branch>` — never silently fall back to origin/main. Optionally keep the main-relative figure as a clearly separate line (`Ahead of origin/main by 98`), since that is useful context for the eventual merge, but it must not be the line labelled "Remote".
findings.effort: Small — approximately 10 lines in one function; the sv script picks up the corrected value with no change.

$ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py 2>&1 | sed -n '/## KEY FILES/,$p' | grep -E "reference_runner|Operational_Plan|launcher"
NEITHER reference_runner_v2.py NOR the operational tracker appears

Both copies of the tracker exist and are current:
$ ls -la ~/Desktop/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md
-rw-r--r--@ 1 georgejackson  staff  153452 Aug  5 14:18 /Users/georgejackson/Desktop/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md
-rw-r--r--@ 1 georgejackson  staff  153452 Aug  5 14:18 experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md

RECOVERY.md itself already says to read it first:
$ python3 -c "...read_section(RECOVERY.md,'## Minimum Recovery','\n## ')..."
(2 minutes)
**First read (added 22 April 2026):** `experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md` (repo mirror) or `~/Desktop/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md` (canonical copy). The operational plan names the exact resume pointer for the Exp 40-54 arc + Bench Run 2 ...

All 14 KEY FILES entries that ARE listed do exist:

findings.root_cause: The `key_files` list at scripts/cdsfl_recover.py:120-135 was written on 8 April 2026 and has not been revised since. The tracker convention was introduced on 22 April 2026 (per the RECOVERY.md line quoted above), two weeks after the script was frozen, and nothing updates the list when a new load-bearing resource is added. The same staleness shows in the runner entries: the list points at bench/experiment_11_orchestrator.py (65,859 bytes) and bench/runner_core.py but not bench/reference_runner_v2.py (447,395 bytes, modified 4 August), which project memory records as the ACTIVE runner for the Exp 40-54 arc.
findings.consequence: The founder's `rs` command is the designated post-compaction entry point, and global policy `operational-tracker-compaction-order` states the tracker must be read end-to-end BEFORE anything else because it alone names the exact resume pointer. An agent that runs `rs` and does exactly what the spec says — rebuild context from output — is never told the tracker exists. Combined with F2 and F3, the output names no current experiment, no pending work, and no resume pointer: the three things a resume actually needs. The stale runner entry compounds it by pointing a recovering agent at the frozen v1-era orchestrator instead of the 447KB active runner.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a dedicated section printed FIRST, before `## CURRENT STATE`, not a fourteenth entry in a list at the bottom: `## FIRST READ` naming `~/Desktop/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md` (canonical) and `experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md` (repo mirror), with each path existence-checked and its mtime printed so staleness is visible, plus a one-line note that it holds the resume pointer. Add `bench/reference_runner_v2.py` to key_files with the description "ACTIVE runner, Exp 40-54" and relabel `bench/experiment_11_orchestrator.py` as v1-era. A cheap guard against recurrence: have scripts/cdsfl_qc.py assert that every path named in RECOVERY.md's Minimum Recovery section also appears in cdsfl_recover.py's key_files.
findings.effort: Small — approximately 12 lines in cdsfl_recover.py; the qc guard is optional and separate.

findings.title: _run_git ignores every git exit code, so a failed remote measurement is reported as "up to date" — currently latent, and the exact Wolfram-401-as-success shape
findings.evidence:
$ python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from cdsfl_utils import _run_git
... out = _run_git('rev-list','--count','origin/does_not_exist..HEAD')
... print('stdout for a FAILING rev-list =', repr(out))
... print('isdigit() ->', out.isdigit(), '=> ahead_n would be', int(out) if out.isdigit() else 0)"
stdout for a FAILING rev-list = ''
isdigit() -> False => ahead_n would be 0

$ git rev-list --count origin/does_not_exist..HEAD
fatal: ambiguous argument 'origin/does_not_exist..HEAD': unknown revision or path not in the working tree.
git exit code = 128

With both counts silently 0, scripts/cdsfl_utils.py:70-71 takes the branch `if ahead_n == 0 and behind_n == 0: remote_sync = "up to date"`. A git process that died with exit 128 and printed a fatal error to stderr is rendered as the reassuring string "up to date".
findings.root_cause: scripts/cdsfl_utils.py:36-45 `_run_git` returns `result.stdout.strip()` and never inspects `result.returncode` or `result.stderr`. Line 68 then converts a non-digit (i.e. failed) result to 0 via `int(ahead) if ahead.isdigit() else 0`. The `_run_git("fetch", "--quiet")` at line 65 is likewise unchecked, so running `rs` offline leaves the remote-tracking refs stale and the ahead/behind figures are computed against whatever was last fetched, with no indication that no fetch occurred.
findings.consequence: Not currently producing a wrong answer here — origin/main exists and the fetch succeeded — which is why this is filed as latent rather than blocking. It fires the moment any of these hold: no network (fetch silently skipped, stale counts presented as current), the remote renamed or the default branch not called main (both counts 0, "up to date" printed having measured nothing), or a shallow/detached checkout. A recovery script that says "up to date" when it measured nothing is the failure that does not look like a failure, and it sits in the same function as F4, so it should be fixed in the same edit.
findings.proposed_fix: Give `_run_git` a `check: bool = False` parameter that returns a sentinel (e.g. `None`) when `result.returncode != 0`, and have git_state() call the remote comparisons with it. When a count is unavailable, set `remote_sync = "UNKNOWN — <git command> failed (exit <n>): <first line of stderr>"` rather than falling through to "up to date". Do the same for the fetch: if it fails, prefix the remote line with `(fetch failed — figures may be stale)`. The rule already written in the project's own .claude/CLAUDE.md for Wolfram applies verbatim: a call that errored did not verify anything.
findings.effort: Small — approximately 8 lines, same function as F4, fix them together.

findings.title: --full prints a bare "2556 tests collected" without the collection-versus-pass caveat that CURRENT_STATE.md carries three sections earlier in the same output
findings.evidence:
$ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py --full 2>&1 | sed -n '/## TESTS/,/## PENDING/p'
## TESTS

  2556 tests collected

## PENDING WORK

Whereas the CURRENT_STATE.md text echoed at the top of the very same run says:
"**2556 tests collected** ... This is a COLLECTION count, not a pass count, and it says nothing about whether the run was offline. Quote it only with the timestamp and commit above. ... Figures labelled \"non-network\" before 2026-07-31 were hand-curated exclusions and included live model dispatch — do not quote them as offline results."

Confirmed --full differs from the default by exactly this block and nothing else:
$ diff plain.txt full.txt
1c1
< CDSFL Recovery — 2026-08-05T14:34:01+01:00
---
> CDSFL Recovery — 2026-08-05T14:34:03+01:00
88a89,92
> ## TESTS
> 
>   2556 tests collected
> 
$ time python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py --full
5.519 total  (docstring claims "~10s")
findings.root_cause: scripts/cdsfl_recover.py:104 prints `f"  {count} tests collected"` with no qualifier. cdsfl_utils.test_count() runs `pytest --co -q` and regex-matches `(\d+)\s+tests?\s+collected`, discarding the return code entirely (line 95-107), so a collection that succeeded with errors would still yield a number. The sv script solved the same problem properly in 2026-07-31 prose but that prose lives only in CURRENT_STATE.md, not in the shared helper.
findings.consequence: Low but not zero, given this project's documented history: a suite was labelled "non-network" for 99 days while making live billed model calls, and the correction note explicitly forbids quoting collection counts as pass counts. The recover output presents the number stripped of every guard, in a section headed simply TESTS, in the document an agent is told to rebuild context from. The most likely downstream error is a note or commit message asserting "2556 tests passing".
findings.proposed_fix: Change line 104 to `print(f"  {count} tests COLLECTED (not a pass count, not an offline result) — for a pass count run: python3 -m pytest bench/tests/ -q --netguard-strict")`. Separately, in cdsfl_utils.test_count(), capture `result.returncode` and return None (or a flagged value) when it is non-zero, so a collection that errored cannot be reported as a clean number.
findings.effort: Trivial — 1 line, plus 2 lines in test_count().

verdicts.title: CURRENT_STATE.md snapshot is one sv-commit stale and is echoed above a contradicting live git block
verdicts.reproduction: $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py — the CURRENT STATE echo prints 'Last commit: `686c515`' / 'Remote: diverged (ahead 97, behind 1)' / 7 uncommitted files, while the GIT STATE block 20 lines below prints 'Last commit: 624b39a' / 'ahead 98, behind 1' / 1 uncommitted file. $ git show --name-only --format='commit %h' 624b39a — returns the 9 files of 624b39a, which include all 7 the snapshot calls uncommitted plus docs/CURRENT_STATE.md itself. I then went further than the auditor and checked history rather than sampling forward: $ for c in 624b39a 9cd8f62 9396c43; do git show $c:docs/CURRENT_STATE.md | grep -m3 -E 'Last commit|Generated|Remote'; done — 624b39a names parent 686c515, 9cd8f62 names parent 4f5adf0, 9396c43 names parent 154d8fc. The 'every single sv' claim holds on every commit I sampled. Root cause verified: $ grep -n 'gs = git_state\|generate_current_state\|_commit_and_push' scripts/cdsfl_sv.py → 724, 738, 809, in that order, so the hash cannot exist when the file is written.
verdicts.correction: Substance, root cause and proposed fix all stand; the fix (label the snapshot, print live GIT STATE first, diff the hashes) addresses the root cause without rewriting history, and would not break anything. Two calibrations on severity. (a) The snapshot is not undated — it carries 'Generated: 5 August 2026 14:08 BST' and was accurate at that instant, and the same run prints the correcting live block, so this is not the fully-silent Wolfram-401 shape; the contradiction is visible in one screen. (b) The project has already applied exactly the auditor's remedy once, by hand: $ git show 122bf64 -- docs/CURRENT_STATE.md shows an inserted note reading that the Git and Experiment sections 'remain the 28 July snapshot and will refresh at the next sv'. That precedent supports the fix and argues the class is understood, not unknown. BLOCKING is defensible only because the fabricated dirty-file list is actively actionable; the rest of the section is stale-but-dated.

verdicts.title: latest_experiment() returns None because two report-less exp53 dirs shadow all 58 archives
verdicts.reproduction: $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py → '## LATEST EXPERIMENT / (No experiment logs found)'. $ python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');from cdsfl_utils import latest_experiment;print(latest_experiment())" → None. Directory census I ran myself: 328 entries in bench/logs/, 58 matching exp(\d+), distinct numbers [53,49,48,47,46,45,44,43,42,41,40,39,38,37,36,35,34,33,32,31,30,29]; both dirs at max_n=53 (exp53_control_zero_live_20260729T222431Z, exp53_control_zero_live_20260801T005649Z) return an empty list for glob('exp*_report.json'). Descending scan I ran: first hit at n=49, exp49_engineering_exam_live, rounds 7, findings 40, converged_at 6 — a fully populated record one step down. Blast radius reproduced: $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py --dry-run → 'Reading experiment logs... none found' then 'No experiment data — skipping ONBOARDING.md experiment update'; $ git status --porcelain before and after was identical, so the dry run wrote nothing.
verdicts.correction: Finding confirmed, including the wider blast radius. Two corrections. (1) The timeline is imprecise. I traced every commit that changed docs/CURRENT_STATE.md: the Latest Experiment section still read 'exp46_stage6_locationkey_live (#46)' at 122bf64 on 2026-08-01 01:53 and first read 'No experiment logs found.' at 91c6c7d on 2026-08-02 22:02. The 1 August change was a hand edit to the Tests block, not an sv regeneration, so no sv ran between the exp53 archive landing and 2 August. 'Every sv since 29 July' is technically true but the observable damage covers five svs from 2 August, not a week. (2) THE PROPOSED FIX IS DEFECTIVE AS WRITTEN and would ship a new silent falsehood of the same class. The auditor says to iterate 'for n in sorted({n for n, _ in exp_dirs}, reverse=True)' and then 'run the existing body'. The existing body returns "number": max_n at cdsfl_utils.py:195 and falls back to f"exp{max_n}" at :196. If max_n stays bound to the global maximum, the output prints 'Number: 53' beside exp49's rounds, findings and gamma. The loop variable must replace max_n throughout the body. (3) Even correctly implemented, the descent silently substitutes exp49 for exp53 as 'LATEST EXPERIMENT' when exp53 genuinely ran and genuinely is newest by mtime — the display must name which experiment it fell back to and that the newest one carried no report, or the repair reproduces the original failure shape one directory further down.

verdicts.title: Remote sync is measured against origin/main, not the branch's upstream, so a fully synchronised branch reports 'diverged (ahead 98, behind 1)'
verdicts.reproduction: $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py → 'Branch: exp39-experimental / Remote: diverged (ahead 98, behind 1)'. $ git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u} → origin/exp39-experimental. $ git rev-list --count origin/exp39-experimental..HEAD → 0; $ git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/exp39-experimental → 0. $ git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD → 98; $ git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main → 1. $ git config --get branch.exp39-experimental.remote → origin; $ git config --get branch.exp39-experimental.merge → refs/heads/exp39-experimental. Source confirmed at scripts/cdsfl_utils.py:66-67, both counts hard-coded to origin/main, with branch already available at :52. The same false figure is frozen into the committed record: $ git show 624b39a:docs/CURRENT_STATE.md | grep Remote → '- **Remote:** diverged (ahead 97, behind 1)'.
verdicts.correction: Defect and root cause both stand exactly as described, and the proposed fix (resolve @{u} first, label the ref used, say 'no upstream configured' rather than falling back) is correct and would not break the no-upstream case. One consequence is overstated: 'a recovering agent would reach for git pull / fetch && rebase / push, and two of those are history-altering'. All three resolve against branch.exp39-experimental.merge = refs/heads/exp39-experimental, which I measured at ahead 0 / behind 0, so all three are no-ops here — the alarm misleads but does not itself endanger the 98 commits. The consequence that does hold, and is the reason this stays BLOCKING rather than cosmetic, is the masking one the auditor also states: because the string depends only on origin/main, genuine unpushed work on the branch cannot change it. In a project whose persistence mechanism is `cdsfl_sv.py --commit --push`, a remote line that cannot report unpushed work is reporting nothing while looking like a report.

verdicts.title: The operational tracker appears nowhere in the recovery output
verdicts.reproduction: $ grep -c 'Operational_Plan\|Agent_Operational' scripts/cdsfl_recover.py → 0, exit 1. Both tracker copies exist and are current: $ ls -la ~/Desktop/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md → both 153452 bytes, Aug 5 14:18. RECOVERY.md's own Minimum Recovery section does name it first (read_section returns 1474 chars whose first substantive line is '**First read (added 22 April 2026):** experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md ...'). $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py | sed -n '/## KEY FILES/,$p' | grep -c '^  ! ' → 0, so every listed path resolves. bench/reference_runner_v2.py (447395 bytes, Aug 4 02:50) is indeed absent from key_files.
verdicts.correction: The omission is real but the severity and one supporting claim are wrong. (a) THE SUPPORTING CLAIM IS FALSE. The auditor says the list 'points a recovering agent at the frozen v1-era orchestrator instead of the 447KB active runner'. bench/experiment_11_orchestrator.py is not v1-era and is not frozen: $ grep -n 'from experiment_11_orchestrator import' bench/reference_runner_v2.py → line 53, i.e. the active v2 runner imports it, and $ git log -1 -- bench/experiment_11_orchestrator.py → 122bf64, 2026-08-01. Its listed description 'Model dispatch and configuration' is accurate — it holds call_openrouter and call_gemini, imported by nine other modules. The project memory note the auditor is leaning on distinguishes reference_runner.py (v1, frozen) from reference_runner_v2.py; it says nothing about the orchestrator. Relabelling the orchestrator 'v1-era' would introduce a false statement into the very list being repaired. (b) SEVERITY. Unlike F1–F4 this section reports nothing false — every path it prints exists, and it prints resources/RECOVERY.md, whose Minimum Recovery section names the tracker as first read. The pointer chain to the tracker survives; it is one hop long instead of zero. That is staleness, not a silent falsehood, and does not warrant BLOCKING alongside a fabricated dirty-file list and a false remote state. (c) The fix is otherwise sound — add a FIRST READ section and add reference_runner_v2.py — but drop the orchestrator relabel, and the cdsfl_qc.py cross-check guard is a good idea worth keeping.

verdicts.title: _run_git ignores exit codes, so a failed remote measurement renders as 'up to date'
verdicts.reproduction: $ python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');from cdsfl_utils import _run_git;out=_run_git('rev-list','--count','origin/does_not_exist..HEAD');print(repr(out), out.isdigit())" → '' False. $ git rev-list --count origin/does_not_exist..HEAD → fatal: ambiguous argument, exit 128. I then closed the loop end-to-end rather than reasoning about the branch, monkeypatching only the rev-list calls to route through that genuinely failing git invocation: git_state()['remote_sync'] → 'up to date'. Two git processes that exited 128 and printed a fatal error render as the reassuring string. $ grep -n 'returncode' scripts/cdsfl_utils.py → no matches anywhere in the file, so no caller inspects any exit status.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed, and the end-to-end demonstration is stronger than the auditor's (they showed the ingredient, I showed the dish). The proposed fix is correct and sits in the right place. Two notes. The 'purely latent' framing is mildly optimistic: the unchecked _run_git('fetch','--quiet') at :65 fires on every run, so an offline `rs` already presents last-fetched counts as current with no indication no fetch occurred — that is a live silent-staleness path today, not a hypothetical. Second, F6 and F4 are the same edit but not the same bug; fixing F4 by resolving @{u} does not fix F6, because a failed rev-list against a valid upstream still degrades to 'up to date'. Fix both or the repair is half-done.

verdicts.title: --full prints a bare '2556 tests collected' without the collection-versus-pass caveat
verdicts.reproduction: $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py --full | sed -n '/## TESTS/,/## PENDING/p' → '## TESTS' / '  2556 tests collected' / '## PENDING WORK'. Diff of the two runs confirms --full adds exactly that block and nothing else (only the timestamp line and lines 89–92 differ). Wall clock 5.640s total against the docstring's '~10s'. $ grep -n 'returncode' scripts/cdsfl_utils.py → no matches, so test_count() at :91-109 genuinely never inspects the exit status.
verdicts.correction: Real but below the LOW bar, and it is not the failure class this audit exists to catch. The printed line says 'collected', which is precisely and truthfully what the number is — no false statement is emitted, unlike F1, F2, F3 and F4. The claimed downstream error ('a note asserting 2556 tests passing') requires a reader to ignore the word actually printed; that is a hardening suggestion, not a spec-vs-behaviour divergence. The proposed one-line change is harmless and I would not object to it, but filing it alongside four genuine silent falsehoods dilutes the report. The returncode sub-claim is the more interesting half and it is source-verified, but I could NOT demonstrate it by execution: I tried to induce a collection error read-only ($ python3 -m pytest bench/tests/ bench/test_falsifier_matrix_2026-06-06.py --co -q → exit 0, 2556 collected, no error path available), and constructing one would have required writing a broken test file, which the read-only constraint forbids. Recorded as unproven by execution.

missed: M1 — SPEC-VS-BEHAVIOUR: the script's own docstring at scripts/cdsfl_recover.py:8 states 'Designed to be fast and read-only', but git_state() runs _run_git('fetch','--quiet') at scripts/cdsfl_utils.py:65, which is a network call that mutates the repository. Demonstrated: $ stat -f '%N mtime=%Sm' .git/FETCH_HEAD → 'Aug 5 14:48:02'; $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py >/dev/null; $ stat -f '%N mtime=%Sm' .git/FETCH_HEAD → 'Aug 5 14:48:36'. One run of the 'read-only' recovery script rewrote .git/FETCH_HEAD and can advance remote-tracking refs. Two consequences the auditor did not draw: `rs` is not safe to characterise as read-only in documentation or to an agent reasoning about side effects, and because that fetch's exit code is discarded (F6), running `rs` with no network silently produces figures computed against whatever was last fetched, presented with no staleness marker. The auditor examined git_state() closely enough to find F4 and F6 in the same function and did not report that the function violates the calling script's stated contract.

M2 — SAME CONFLATION CLASS AS F3, INSIDE THE FUNCTION F2 IS ABOUT, UNREPORTED: latest_experiment() swallows corruption at scripts/cdsfl_utils.py:210-211 ('except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError): continue') and then returns None at :213, so a corrupt or unreadable report is indistinguishable from an absent one, and cdsfl_recover.py:97 prints the identical '(No experiment logs found)' for both. Demonstrated in memory with no writes, by patching json.loads to raise JSONDecodeError for every report: latest_experiment() → None, byte-identical to today's real absent-report result, which I printed alongside it in the same run. This matters because the auditor's own F2 fix proposal ('return a marker such as {error: N experiment dirs scanned, none carried an exp*_report.json}') would print a message that is FALSE in the corruption case — the dirs did carry report files, they were unparseable. Any repair must distinguish three states, not two: no exp dirs / dirs present but no report file / report file present but unreadable. Reporting a parse failure as 'none carried a report' is the same shape as the verdict reader that matched 'NOT FALSIFIED' as 'FALSIFIED'.

M3 — HEADLINE UNDERCOUNT (minor, but it is the sentence a reader will quote): the auditor's headline says 'three sections silently false or empty (git snapshot, latest experiment, pending work)'. By the auditor's own F4, the live GIT STATE section is also false — its Remote line reads 'diverged (ahead 98, behind 1)' against an upstream I measured at ahead 0 / behind 0. Four of the seven sections carry a false or empty statement, not three: CURRENT STATE (stale by construction), GIT STATE (false remote line), LATEST EXPERIMENT (false negative), PENDING WORK (false negative). RECENT COMMITS and KEY FILES are accurate, and TESTS is accurate but uncaveated.

report.headline: The commit and push work, but the state snapshot sv exists to produce is wrong in four independent ways at once — it names the wrong commit (8 of 8 commits checked), reports a clean tree as DIRTY, has silently reported "No experiment logs found" for the last five saves while 40+ experiment logs sit on disk, and prints a false remote-sync verdict — and two clauses of the spec (Open Brain capture, memory-file update) are not implemented in the script at all.

findings.title: CURRENT_STATE.md is generated before the commit, so it structurally can never describe the commit that carries it — 8 of 8 commits checked name the parent and claim DIRTY
findings.evidence:
Source ordering: `gs = git_state()` at line 724; `state_content = generate_current_state(gs, ...)` at line 738; `state_path.write_text(state_content)` at line 747; `_commit_and_push(...)` not called until line 809 (the actual `git commit` runs at line 678). Nothing regenerates the file afterwards.

Command: `for c in $(git log --format=%h -8 -- docs/CURRENT_STATE.md); do parent=$(git rev-parse --short ${c}^); named=$(git show $c:docs/CURRENT_STATE.md | grep -m1 'Last commit'); tree=$(git show $c:docs/CURRENT_STATE.md | grep -m1 'Working tree'); printf "commit %s parent %s | %s | %s\n" "$c" "$parent" "$named" "$tree"; done`

Output (8/8 wrong):
commit 624b39a parent 686c515 | - **Last commit:** `686c515` ... | - **Working tree:** DIRTY
commit 9396c43 parent 154d8fc | - **Last commit:** `154d8fc` ... | - **Working tree:** DIRTY
commit 9cd8f62 parent 4f5adf0 | - **Last commit:** `4f5adf0` ... | - **Working tree:** DIRTY
commit 8690467 parent 448b3e4 | - **Last commit:** `448b3e4` ... | - **Working tree:** DIRTY
commit 91c6c7d parent 439d18f | - **Last commit:** `439d18f` ... | - **Working tree:** DIRTY
commit 122bf64 parent d4d4d7f | - **Last commit:** `8c7fe3e` ... | - **Working tree:** DIRTY   <-- two commits behind
commit ea3546d parent 8c7fe3e | - **Last commit:** `8c7fe3e` ... | - **Working tree:** DIRTY
commit c0904ae parent 71d00be | - **Last commit:** `71d00be` ... | - **Working tree:** DIRTY

The live self-contradiction, `python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py`, in a single output:
  ## CURRENT STATE  ->  "- **Last commit:** `686c515` ..."  "- **Working tree:** DIRTY — uncommitted changes present" followed by 7 filenames
  ## GIT STATE     ->  "Last commit: 624b39a sv: PROVENANCE CORRECTION..."  "Uncommitted: M experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md" (1 file)

Also measured: commit 122bf64 (dated 2026-08-01) carries a CURRENT_STATE.md whose header reads `Generated: 28 July 2026 20:09 BST` — three days stale at commit time, swept in by `git add -u` without sv having been re-run.
findings.root_cause: The snapshot is built from a git state read at line 724, i.e. before staging and before `git commit`. The seven files it lists as "uncommitted" are precisely the files the commit is about to contain. There is no post-commit regeneration or amend step, so the file is wrong at the instant it is created and stays wrong until the next sv — at which point it is wrong about that commit instead.
findings.consequence: This is the root cause of the recover script's self-contradiction, and it is the guaranteed part of it (ageing between saves only widens an error that already exists at t=0). `cdsfl_recover.py` prints CURRENT_STATE.md verbatim as its FIRST section, before any live git state, so a compacted agent rebuilding context reads the wrong HEAD first and reads it as authoritative. Right now that agent would believe HEAD is 686c515 (one behind), that the tree is dirty with 7 files, and that 7 files of work are unsaved when they are in fact committed. The two most likely reactions — re-doing committed work, or treating committed work as unsaved and re-staging it — both cost time or damage state. Worse for a `git clone` recovery: the committed copy is the only copy, and it can never be right.
findings.proposed_fix: Reorder to: stage -> commit -> regenerate CURRENT_STATE.md from post-commit git state -> `git add docs/CURRENT_STATE.md` -> `git commit --amend --no-edit` -> push. The amend is safe because push is step 9, after the commit, so nothing has left the machine yet. If amending is unwanted, the zero-risk alternative is to stop asserting what the file cannot know: replace the `Last commit` / `Working tree` block with an explicit banner — "Snapshot taken immediately BEFORE the commit that carries this file. The hash below is that commit's PARENT; the files listed as uncommitted are the contents of that commit." — which removes the false reading at the cost of one paragraph.
findings.effort: Small — about 10 lines for the amend path, or 3 lines for the banner.

findings.title: The whole Latest Experiment section has silently read "No experiment logs found" for the last five state saves, because two report-less exp53 directories suppress the entire lookup
findings.evidence:
Command: `python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py --dry-run`
Output: "Reading experiment logs... none found" ... "Latest exp: none"

Root-cause probe (read-only python over bench/logs):
  max experiment number found: 53
  dirs at max_n: exp53_control_zero_live_20260729T222431Z -> report files: 0
                 exp53_control_zero_live_20260801T005649Z -> report files: 0
  dirs that DO have a report, top 5 by number: 49, 48, 47, 46, 45

Source: `max_n = max(n for n, _ in exp_dirs)` (line 133); `candidates` is filtered to `n == max_n` only (lines 134-138); the `for exp_dir in candidates` loop `continue`s when no `exp*_report.json` is present (lines 142-144); falling out of that loop returns None at line 213. There is no fallback to the next-highest experiment number.

Historical confirmation: `for c in $(git log --format=%h -12 -- docs/CURRENT_STATE.md); do ... sed -n '/## Latest Experiment/,+3p' ...` gives
  624b39a 2026-08-05 | No experiment logs found.
  9396c43 2026-08-04 | No experiment logs found.
  9cd8f62 2026-08-04 | No experiment logs found.
  8690467 2026-08-02 | No experiment logs found.
  91c6c7d 2026-08-02 | No experiment logs found.
  122bf64 2026-08-01 | - **Experiment:** exp46_stage6_locationkey_live (#46)
Live file, `sed -n '/## Latest Experiment/,/## Recent Commits/p' docs/CURRENT_STATE.md`:
  ## Latest Experiment
  No experiment logs found.
findings.root_cause: `latest_experiment()` picks the single highest experiment NUMBER, then searches only directories carrying that number. The exp53 control runs halted before writing a report, so both exp53 directories lack `exp*_report.json`. The function returns None rather than falling back to exp49, which has a complete report. The failure then presents as the innocuous-looking sentence "No experiment logs found."
findings.consequence: Every state save since 2026-08-02 22:02 has published a recovery snapshot asserting that no experiment logs exist, in a repository containing 40+ experiment log directories including five converged runs. It also disables two further sv steps: the ONBOARDING.md experiment-summary update is skipped entirely ("No experiment data — skipping ONBOARDING.md experiment update") and RECOVERY.md's pending-work block loses its experiment stanza. A compacted agent reading CURRENT_STATE.md would conclude the experimental arc has produced nothing — the exact opposite of the record. The sentence is indistinguishable from the legitimate case of a fresh clone with no runs yet.
findings.proposed_fix: Iterate experiment numbers in descending order and return the first number that yields a parseable report, instead of returning None after the highest number fails. Separately, make the two cases distinguishable in the output: if `bench/logs/` contains exp directories but none parse, CURRENT_STATE.md must say "N experiment directories found, none carrying a parseable report (highest: exp53)" — never "No experiment logs found."
findings.effort: Small — restructure one loop, about 8 lines, plus one output string.

findings.title: sv captures nothing to Open Brain, so the global spec's "Open Brain session summary" is an unenforced manual step — and it has been missed for the last two saves
findings.evidence:
Command: `grep -rn "open_brain\|Open Brain\|OpenBrain\|capture_memory\|session-context" scripts/cdsfl_sv.py scripts/cdsfl_utils.py` -> exit 1, no matches. `grep -rln "Desktop" scripts/ .claude/` -> only `scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py` (a claude.ai download URL) and settings/CLAUDE.md; no sv path.

Open Brain's actual contents, `mcp__open_brain__list_recent(limit=8)`, newest first:
  1. created_at 2026-08-02T22:20:50+01:00  "CDSFL sv 2026-08-02 22:20 BST ... HEAD 8690467"
  2. created_at 2026-08-02T22:03:05+01:00  "CDSFL sv 2026-08-02 22:02 BST. HEAD 91c6c7d"
  3. created_at 2026-07-03T00:24:06+01:00

Against the sv commits actually made since: `git log --oneline -5` shows 9396c43 (sv, 2026-08-04) and 624b39a (sv, 2026-08-05). Neither produced an Open Brain entry. Confirmed, not refuted.
findings.root_cause: The global spec defines sv as including an Open Brain session summary, but the script that the project spec names as "the final step" of sv contains no Open Brain code path of any kind. The capture is therefore only as reliable as the agent remembering to do it before running the script — and on 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-05 it was not done.
findings.consequence: Open Brain is one of the two mandated post-compaction recovery reads (`python3 -m open_brain.cli session-context --agent cc`). Its record now ends at 2026-08-02, so it silently omits the entire 2026-08-04/05 arc — the simulated-bench end-to-end run and the provenance correction, which is precisely the material a recovering agent most needs and least expects to be missing. Nothing in the sv output warns about it: sv prints "State save complete." whether or not the capture happened. A recovering agent reads a complete-looking Open Brain history and has no way to know it is three days short.
findings.proposed_fix: Make sv the enforcement point rather than adding cross-repo write code: before committing, query Open Brain for a `session_summary` from `source_agent=cc` created today; if there is none, print a loud blocking warning naming the gap and require an explicit `--no-open-brain` flag to proceed. That keeps the write manual (where the judgement lives) but makes omission impossible to miss. If the founder prefers automation, the alternative is a subprocess call to the Open Brain CLI from the script.
findings.effort: Small for the check (about 15 lines); medium for automated capture.

findings.title: The remote-sync verdict is computed against origin/main rather than the branch's actual upstream — it currently reports "diverged (ahead 98, behind 1)" for a branch that is exactly in sync, and a total failure of the check renders as "up to date"
findings.evidence:
Source: `ahead = _run_git("rev-list", "--count", "origin/main..HEAD")` and `behind = _run_git("rev-list", "--count", "HEAD..origin/main")` (lines 66-67), hardcoded to origin/main; `ahead_n = int(ahead) if ahead.isdigit() else 0` (lines 68-69). `_run_git` (lines 36-45) returns `result.stdout.strip()` and never inspects `returncode`.

Command: `git branch --show-current; git rev-parse --abbrev-ref '@{u}'; git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD; git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main; git rev-list --left-right --count 'origin/exp39-experimental...HEAD'`
Output:
  exp39-experimental
  origin/exp39-experimental
  98
  1
  0	0          <-- the branch is EXACTLY in sync with its real upstream

What sv and recover both print, from `python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py --dry-run`:
  Remote: diverged (ahead 98, behind 1)

The failure-looks-like-success half, executed against a missing ref (exactly what happens on a branch or clone with no origin/main):
  ahead stdout=''  behind stdout=''
  git_state() would report Remote: up to date
findings.root_cause: Two defects compound. (1) The comparison ref is hardcoded to origin/main while the project has worked on exp39-experimental for months, so the number reported is the branch's distance from main, presented under the label "Remote:" with the verdict words "up to date" / "diverged". (2) `_run_git` discards the return code, so a failed `rev-list` yields an empty string, `isdigit()` is False, the count silently becomes 0, and 0/0 renders as the success string "up to date". The `git fetch --quiet` on line 65 is likewise unchecked, so an offline or failed fetch produces a confident verdict from stale refs with no indication.
findings.consequence: This is the project's named failure shape twice over. Today it produces a false alarm: CURRENT_STATE.md and every recover run assert a diverged remote for a branch that is 0/0 with its upstream, inviting a reconcile that is not needed. In the more dangerous direction it produces a false all-clear: on any branch without origin/main, or whenever the rev-list fails, the recovery snapshot reads "Remote: up to date" — the same string it prints when everything genuinely is fine. That directly undermines SV-08 (a commit that was created but failed to push would show only as ahead 99 instead of ahead 98, which no reader can distinguish).
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the upstream with `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}` and compare against that; check every return code and report "unknown (rev-list failed)" or "unknown (no upstream configured)" rather than defaulting to 0. Surface a failed `git fetch` as "remote state not refreshed" instead of silently comparing stale refs. The rule the project already applies to Wolfram applies here unchanged: a failed measurement is not a result.
findings.effort: Small — about 15 lines in git_state().

findings.title: The closing summary always claims ONBOARDING.md and RECOVERY.md were auto-generated, including immediately after printing "Preserved manual content" for both, and including under --dry-run where nothing is written at all
findings.evidence:
Source lines 800-802 are guarded only by `if exp:` and are reached regardless of what the update functions returned:
    if exp:
        print(f"  ONBOARDING.md: experiment #{exp['number']} summary auto-generated")
        print(f"  RECOVERY.md: pending work auto-generated")

Demonstrated by running main() under --dry-run with latest_experiment substituted so the reporting path is reachable (no file written — --dry-run suppresses every write):
  Preserved manual content: /Users/.../resources/ONBOARDING.md
  Preserved manual content: /Users/.../resources/RECOVERY.md

  State save complete.
    Branch: exp39-experimental @ 624b39a
    Latest exp: exp47_divergence
    ONBOARDING.md: experiment #47 summary auto-generated
    RECOVERY.md: pending work auto-generated

The two claims are false in the same output that says the content was preserved, and false again because --dry-run wrote nothing.

This is not an edge case: `grep -n "SV:LATEST_EXP" resources/ONBOARDING.md` gives markers at lines 95 and 1061 — 966 lines of manual content between them — and `grep -n "SV:PENDING" resources/RECOVERY.md` gives 799 and 2375. `_has_manual_content` (line 165) therefore returns True for both files permanently, so `update_onboarding_experiment` and `update_recovery_pending` can only ever return False, and these two lines are unconditionally false whenever an experiment is found.
findings.root_cause: The final summary block re-asserts success from the loop condition (`if exp:`) instead of from the return values of the update functions, which are already computed and already correctly reported 30 lines earlier. The dry-run flag is not consulted at all in the summary.
findings.consequence: The summary block is the part a founder or a compacting agent reads and transcribes — "sv done, ONBOARDING and RECOVERY updated". It is a false claim about the state of the two most load-bearing recovery documents, it fires on every run that finds an experiment, and it will keep firing forever because the manual content in those files means the auto-blocks can never regenerate. An operator who trusts it believes the experiment summary in ONBOARDING.md is current when it is frozen at whatever was last written by hand.
findings.proposed_fix: Capture the booleans returned by `update_onboarding_experiment` and `update_recovery_pending` and print one of three honest lines: "summary regenerated", "manual content preserved — auto-block NOT regenerated", or "unchanged". Prefix the entire summary with "(dry run — nothing written)" when `args.dry_run` is set.
findings.effort: Trivial — about 6 lines.

findings.title: sv does not refresh the repo mirror of the operational tracker from the Desktop canonical, so the canonical and the version-controlled copy can diverge with nothing detecting it
findings.evidence:
Command: `grep -rn "Desktop|Operational_Plan|memory/" scripts/cdsfl_sv.py` -> exit 1, no matches. `grep -rln "Desktop" scripts/ .claude/` -> `scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py` (a claude.ai download URL at line 254), `.claude/settings.json` (an MCP tool glob), `.claude/CLAUDE.md` (prose). No copy or comparison of ~/Desktop/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md anywhere.

sv's staging is: three explicit adds (line 595), `git add -u` (line 600), untracked files under the whitelist (lines 605-611). `git add -u` stages the repo mirror only if it is ALREADY modified in the repo — it cannot pull content across from the Desktop.

Current state, `md5 -q ~/Desktop/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md`:
  198ff2ec7f3c9632ebb23647d66c0e6a
  198ff2ec7f3c9632ebb23647d66c0e6a
Both 153452 bytes, both mtime Aug 5 14:18, diff is empty. So there is NO live divergence today — an agent refreshed the mirror by hand at 14:18, ten minutes after the 14:08 sv. The gap is in the mechanism, not in the current bytes.

Historical trace of the same gap: commit 9396c43's CURRENT_STATE.md lists `M experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md` as uncommitted, and `git diff --stat -- experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md` shows the mirror modified-but-uncommitted right now, after the most recent sv.
findings.root_cause: Policy (`operational-tracker-update-policy`) says the repo mirror is refreshed "at each Phase close or before commit" but does not name an owner, and no code implements it. The refresh is therefore an unenforced habit performed by whichever agent remembers.
findings.consequence: The Desktop file is canonical and is the designated first read after compaction; the repo mirror is what survives a machine loss or a fresh clone. If an agent edits the Desktop copy and does not hand-copy it, sv commits nothing, prints "State save complete", and the repo copy silently ages. A recovery that reaches for the repo — precisely the recovery where the Desktop is unavailable — gets a stale resume pointer with no marker saying so. This needs a ruling because it is a scope question: should sv own the copy, or should it only detect and refuse?
findings.proposed_fix: Minimum: before staging, compare the two files and, if they differ, print a loud warning naming which is newer and abort the commit unless `--allow-tracker-drift` is passed. Stronger, and probably right given the Desktop copy is defined as canonical: copy Desktop -> repo mirror before staging, and print the byte delta so the copy is visible in the sv output. Founder ruling needed on which.
findings.effort: Small — about 12 lines either way.

findings.title: sv never touches the persistent-memory directory; "update memory files" is entirely a manual agent step with no check
findings.evidence:
Command: `grep -rn "\.claude/projects|memory/MEMORY|MEMORY.md" scripts/` -> exit 1, no matches anywhere in scripts/. The memory directory is outside the repository, at /Users/georgejackson/.claude/projects/-Users-georgejackson-Developer-Projects/memory/, so `git add -u` cannot reach it either.

It did happen this time, by hand: `ls -lt` on that directory shows MEMORY.md at Aug 5 14:04 and cdsfl_session_2026-08-01.md at Aug 5 14:05, both just before the 14:08 sv commit. But nothing in the script caused or verified that.

Stating it plainly, as asked: the memory-file update is MANUAL. The script does not read, write, check or mention those files.
findings.root_cause: The spec clause "update memory files" is assigned to the operator, not the script, and the script provides no verification hook. Its reliability equals the agent's memory — the same failure mode that produced the missing Open Brain entries in SV-03, which did in fact occur twice in the last two saves.
findings.consequence: Memory files and Open Brain are the two recovery channels that survive when the repo is not the thing being read. Both currently depend on an agent remembering, and one of the two has already been missed twice this week. Because sv prints "State save complete" regardless, an omission produces no signal at any point.
findings.proposed_fix: Same pattern as SV-03: a preflight check, not automation. Before committing, stat the memory directory; if no file has been modified since the previous sv commit's timestamp, print a loud warning and require an explicit override flag. This preserves the judgement (what to write) while removing the silence (whether anything was written). Founder ruling needed on whether sv should gate on out-of-repo state at all.
findings.effort: Small — about 12 lines.

findings.title: The push runs after the commit and is not atomic despite the spec's wording; a push timeout escapes the error handler entirely, and a failed push leaves a clean tree that reads as "saved"
findings.evidence:
Source: `_git("commit", ...)` at line 678, then `if push:` / `_git("push", "origin", branch, timeout=120)` at lines 684-686. Any push failure raises RuntimeError from `_git` (line 508), caught at line 821, printing "ERROR: ..." and exiting 1 — after the commit already exists locally.

Timeout is a different class and is not caught. Executed:
  B) timeout is NOT a RuntimeError, so main()'s handler does not catch it:
     escapes as TimeoutExpired - main() only catches RuntimeError
(from calling `_git("log","--oneline","-1", timeout=0)` and catching RuntimeError first, then Exception). `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` inherits SubprocessError, not RuntimeError, so a push that exceeds 120 s produces a raw traceback rather than the intended error path.

The project spec at .claude/CLAUDE.md line 8 claims the script "atomically commits + pushes in a single subprocess (compaction-safe)". Single subprocess: true. Atomic: false — the commit survives a failed push. The script's own docstring (line 5) documents only `[--dry-run]` and never mentions --commit or --push, the flags the spec instructs the operator to use.
findings.root_cause: Commit and push are sequential git operations with no compensating action, and the failure handler covers only one of the two exception families that `_git` can raise.
findings.consequence: After a failed or timed-out push the repository is left with a local commit and a clean working tree. If the session compacts at that moment — which is the exact scenario sv exists to survive — the next agent runs `git status`, sees "clean", and concludes the save completed. SV-04 removes the remaining safety net: the ahead-count is measured against origin/main, so an unpushed commit moves the reading from "ahead 98" to "ahead 99", which no reader can distinguish. The word "atomically" in the spec actively encourages the wrong assumption.
findings.proposed_fix: Catch `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` alongside RuntimeError at line 821. On any post-commit failure, print an unmissable line naming the exact recovery command — "COMMIT <hash> CREATED BUT NOT PUSHED. Run: git push origin <branch>" — rather than a bare ERROR. Correct the word "atomically" in .claude/CLAUDE.md to "commits, then pushes", and add --commit/--push to the script docstring.
findings.effort: Trivial — about 8 lines plus a docs line.

findings.title: The auto-stage loop runs git add with check=False and prints the file as staged whether or not the add succeeded; files outside the whitelist are dropped with no mention at all
findings.evidence:
Source lines 608-611:
    print(f"  Auto-staging {len(untracked)} untracked file(s) under whitelist:")
    for rel in untracked:
        _git("add", "--", rel, root=root, check=False)
        print(f"    + {rel}")
The print is unconditional and the add cannot report failure.

Demonstrated that check=False makes failure indistinguishable from success (read-only git command used so nothing is staged):
  A) check=False swallows a git failure and returns a normal value:
     returned ''  (no exception raised; caller cannot distinguish this from success)

What the whitelist actually covers, running the real predicate from the module against this repo's real layout:
  .claude/CLAUDE.md                auto-staged if untracked: False
  README.md                        auto-staged if untracked: False
  PAPER.md                         auto-staged if untracked: False
  pytest.ini                       auto-staged if untracked: False
  falsify_verify_bundle.py         auto-staged if untracked: False
  experimental_notes/x.md          auto-staged if untracked: True
  bench/y.py                       auto-staged if untracked: True

Full staging set, for the record: three explicit adds (line 595), `git add -u` covering ALL tracked modifications repo-wide (line 600, so it is not a curated list for modifications), plus untracked files under bench/ configs/ docs/ examples/ experimental_notes/ logs/ resources/ scripts/ only.

No live loss today: `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` partitions to 0 inside the whitelist and 0 outside — there are currently no untracked files at all. One collision exists in the sensitive filter: `.env.example` is tracked and matches the `.env` substring, so any modification to it would be staged by `git add -u` then unstaged again (with a printed WARNING) at line 622.
findings.root_cause: `check=False` was presumably chosen so one bad path cannot abort the whole save, but the compensating report was never added; and the whitelist, which is a deliberate and reasonable safety choice, announces only what it staged and never what it skipped.
findings.consequence: A new top-level note, a new file under .claude/, or an add that fails for any reason is omitted from the sv commit while sv prints "State save committed and pushed." This is the silent-data-loss shape rather than a live defect — the mechanism is demonstrated, but no file is currently affected, and I could not exercise the end-to-end path because it requires a write.
findings.proposed_fix: Use check=True for the add, or capture the return code and print "+ <path>" only on success and "! FAILED TO STAGE <path>" otherwise. Separately, compute the untracked files that fell OUTSIDE the whitelist and print them under a heading such as "NOT staged (outside whitelist — stage manually if intended)", so the exclusion is a visible decision rather than a silence.
findings.effort: Trivial — about 8 lines.

findings.title: RECOVERY.md's generated pending-work block hardcodes "Experiments 12-N ALL COMPLETE" regardless of the latest experiment's status
findings.evidence:
Source line 251: `f"Experiments 12–{n} ALL COMPLETE. {tests or '?'} tests collected at {ts} "` — the phrase is a literal, with no reference to `status`.

Called directly with a diverged experiment (pure function, no writes):
  ## Current Pending Work (5 August 2026 14:34 BST)

  Experiments 12–47 ALL COMPLETE. 2556 tests collected at 5 August 2026 14:34 BST (collection count, not a pass count — see docs/CURRENT_STATE.md).

  EXP 47 DIVERGED (5 August 2026 14:34 BST):
    Target: bench/x.py, star, 16 rounds.
    40 findings, γ=0.210. no convergence; max rounds hit.

The block asserts completion and divergence three lines apart. Note also that the parenthesised timestamp on the EXP line is the sv run time, not the experiment's own timestamp (the dict's `timestamp` field is never used), so a recovery doc dates every experiment to the moment of the save.

Currently DORMANT: RECOVERY.md carries manual content between its SV:PENDING markers (lines 799-2375), so `_has_manual_content` returns True and this block is never written. `python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py --dry-run` confirms: "Preserved manual content: /Users/.../resources/RECOVERY.md".
findings.root_cause: A summary sentence that was true when written was frozen as a literal rather than derived from the experiment status that the same function already has in hand.
findings.consequence: If RECOVERY.md's auto-block ever becomes live again — a reset of the markers, a placeholder restored, a fresh clone whose RECOVERY.md still has the placeholder — sv writes a false completion claim into the recovery document, in the same paragraph as the contradicting status. Latent rather than active, and cheap to close now.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the sentence from status: "Experiments 12-N complete" only when the latest experiment converged; otherwise "Experiments 12-{n-1} complete; EXP {n} {status}". Use the experiment's own `timestamp` field on the EXP line instead of the sv run time.
findings.effort: Trivial — 3 lines.

The gate itself currently passes, so nothing is blocked today: `python3 scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py --dry-run` returns rc=0 with "cdsfl_onboard --dry-run: OK".

findings.consequence: If cdsfl_onboard.py --dry-run ever fails — it is an external dependency that reads ONBOARDING.md and REPRODUCING.md and can break on ordinary doc edits — sv refuses to commit and hands the operator an override that immediately fails with rc=2. Under time pressure, mid-compaction, that turns a recoverable abort into a dead end where a state save cannot be completed at all.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `--skip-onboard-check` to the parser and thread it through to `_commit_and_push`, or delete the sentence from the error message and name a real remedy instead.
findings.effort: Trivial — 4 lines.

verdicts.title: CURRENT_STATE.md generated pre-commit, names the parent and claims DIRTY
verdicts.reproduction: Ran the auditor's loop verbatim: `for c in $(git log --format=%h -8 -- docs/CURRENT_STATE.md); do parent=$(git rev-parse --short ${c}^); named=$(git show $c:docs/CURRENT_STATE.md | grep -m1 'Last commit'); tree=$(git show $c:docs/CURRENT_STATE.md | grep -m1 'Working tree'); printf ...; done`. I saw 8/8 name the parent and 8/8 say DIRTY: 624b39a->686c515, 9396c43->154d8fc, 9cd8f62->4f5adf0, 8690467->448b3e4, 91c6c7d->439d18f, 122bf64 names 8c7fe3e (parent d4d4d7f), ea3546d->8c7fe3e, c0904ae->71d00be. Source ordering verified with `sed -n '715,760p' scripts/cdsfl_sv.py` and `sed -n '795,830p'`: gs=git_state() at 724, generate_current_state at 738, write_text at 747, _commit_and_push not reached until 809; nothing regenerates. Live self-contradiction reproduced with `python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py`: the FIRST section (## CURRENT STATE) prints 'Last commit: 686c515' and 'Working tree: DIRTY' with 7 filenames, while ## GIT STATE 44 lines later prints 'Last commit: 624b39a' and one uncommitted file. Stale-header claim also reproduced: `git show 122bf64:docs/CURRENT_STATE.md | head -5` gives 'Generated: 28 July 2026 20:09 BST' against `git log -1 --format=%ad 122bf64` = 2026-08-01.
verdicts.correction: Finding stands as written. The PROPOSED FIX IS WRONG in its primary form and would make the clone-recovery case worse. commit -> regenerate -> `git add` -> `git commit --amend --no-edit` changes the tree, so the amend mints a new SHA H2 and orphans H1; the CURRENT_STATE.md inside H2 would name H1, which is unreachable from any ref and resolves to 'fatal: bad object' in a fresh clone. That converts 'names the parent (a real, reachable commit)' into 'names a commit that does not exist', which is strictly worse for the git-clone recovery the finding itself flags as the dangerous case. The auditor's stated ALTERNATIVE (drop the assertion, print an explicit banner saying the hash is the parent and the listed files are this commit's contents) is sound and is the fix that should be taken. A correct automated fix would need a two-commit sequence (commit the work, then a second commit carrying the snapshot that names the first) rather than an amend.

HEAD 8690467', (3) 2026-08-02T22:03:05 'CDSFL sv ... HEAD 91c6c7d', (4) 2026-07-03T00:24:06. Against `git log --oneline -5`, the sv commits 9396c43 (2026-08-04) and 624b39a (2026-08-05) have no corresponding entry. The factual gap reproduces.
verdicts.correction: The symptom is real; the attribution and the severity are not. This is not a defect of cdsfl_sv.py. The script's own docstring, lines 19-22, states it plainly: 'This script does NOT read ONBOARDING.md, RECOVERY.md, MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md, PAPER.md or memory files itself — the OPERATOR's qualitative updates must be prepared before the script runs.' The script is documented as the last step of sv, not the whole of it. So there is no spec-vs-behaviour divergence in the resource — there is an operator omission on two days, and a process that has no verification hook. That is exactly the shape the auditor themselves rated NEEDS_RULING for SV-07, which is structurally identical (out-of-repo state, manual step, no check). Rating one BLOCKING and the other NEEDS_RULING is inconsistent; both are NEEDS_RULING. It was live before 2026-08-02 and will go live again the moment SV-02 is fixed, so it is worth closing, but at LOW/NEEDS_RULING, not alongside the two findings that corrupt committed files. The proposed fix is correct. It is also incomplete: the same false-report class fires on the line ABOVE it — update_timestamp (cdsfl_sv.py:441-459) returns True under dry_run without writing, so every `--dry-run` today already prints 'Updated timestamp: .../ONBOARDING.md' and '.../RECOVERY.md' for two files it did not touch. verdicts.title: Push is not atomic with the commit; a push timeout escapes the error handler
verdicts.reproduction: Timeout class verified by execution against a read-only git command: `python3 -c "...import cdsfl_sv; cdsfl_sv._git('log','--oneline','-1', timeout=0)..."` printed 'NOT a RuntimeError -> escapes main() handler. type= TimeoutExpired', 'is subclass of RuntimeError? False', MRO ['TimeoutExpired','SubprocessError','Exception','BaseException','object']. main()'s only handler is `except RuntimeError` (line 821), so a push exceeding the 120 s timeout at line 686 produces a raw traceback. Sequencing verified by source: `_git('commit', ...)` at line 677-678, `_git('push','origin',branch, timeout=120)` at 684-686, no compensating action. Docstring claim verified: `sed -n '1,10p' scripts/cdsfl_sv.py` shows 'Usage: python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py [--dry-run]' with no --commit/--push, while .claude/CLAUDE.md:8 instructs the operator to run it with '--commit --push' and calls the result 'atomically commits + pushes'.
verdicts.correction: Both mechanisms reproduce and LOW is the right severity. One part of the consequence argument is wrong and would mislead whoever acts on it: the claim that after a failed push 'the next agent runs git status, sees clean, and concludes the save completed' is false. `git status` reports upstream divergence against the branch's real upstream, not against origin/main — right now it says 'Your branch is up to date with origin/exp39-experimental', and after an unpushed commit it would say 'ahead of origin/exp39-experimental by 1 commit'. Since the global post-compaction protocol mandates `git log --oneline -5 && git status` as the first check, the signal the finding says is absent is in fact present in the very command a recovering agent is required to run. SV-04 blinds cdsfl_recover.py's Remote line, not git status. The proposed fix (catch TimeoutExpired, print the exact recovery command, correct 'atomically', document the flags) is correct and cheap regardless.

verdicts.title: Auto-stage prints files as staged regardless of whether git add succeeded; out-of-whitelist files dropped silently
verdicts.reproduction: Source at cdsfl_sv.py:608-611 confirms the unconditional print after `_git('add','--',rel, check=False)`. Swallow demonstrated with a read-only failing git command: `python3 -c "...cdsfl_sv._git('rev-parse','--verify','definitely-not-a-ref', check=False)"` returned '' with no exception raised — indistinguishable from success at the call site. Whitelist predicate run against the real constant: _SAFE_STAGING_DIRS = ('bench/','configs/','docs/','examples/','experimental_notes/','logs/','resources/','scripts/'); .claude/CLAUDE.md, README.md, PAPER.md, pytest.ini and falsify_verify_bundle.py all evaluate False, experimental_notes/x.md, bench/y.py, scripts/z.py all True. No live loss: `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` returns empty — there are currently no untracked files at all. The .env.example collision reproduces: it is tracked (`git ls-files | grep -i env`), and the sensitive predicate returns True for it since '.env' is a substring, so a modification would be staged by `git add -u` and then reset with a printed WARNING.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed, correctly rated LOW, and the auditor was honest that no file is currently affected and that the end-to-end path could not be exercised without a write. Worth keeping in mind when fixing: the whitelist governs untracked files only — modifications to .claude/CLAUDE.md, README.md and the other excluded paths are already covered by `git add -u` because those files are tracked, so the exposure is strictly 'a NEW file outside the whitelist', not 'changes to top-level files'. The proposed fix is correct on both halves.

verdicts.title: Abort message names --skip-onboard-check, a flag argparse rejects
verdicts.reproduction: `grep -n "skip-onboard-check" scripts/cdsfl_sv.py` -> single hit at line 666. `python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py --skip-onboard-check --dry-run` -> 'cdsfl_sv.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --skip-onboard-check', rc=2. Gate currently passes: `python3 scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py --dry-run` -> rc=0.
verdicts.correction: The core fact is confirmed — the flag is named in an error string and does not exist. The consequence is attached to the wrong branch, which matters because it changes when the dead end can actually occur. Line 666 sits inside `except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError)` at line 663, i.e. it fires only when cdsfl_onboard.py cannot be EXECUTED at all (timeout, missing interpreter, OS error). The scenario the finding describes — 'it reads ONBOARDING.md and REPRODUCING.md and can break on ordinary doc edits' — is the `if dry.returncode != 0` branch at line 668, whose message is 'Canonical-doc wiring has drifted. Repair ONBOARDING.md / REPRODUCING.md before committing' and which never mentions the flag. So the common failure mode does not hand the operator a broken override; the rare execution failure does. Severity LOW is right; the described dead-end is narrower than claimed. The proposed fix (implement the flag, or delete the sentence) is correct either way — deleting the sentence is the smaller change and loses nothing, since the execution-failure branch has no sensible override anyway.
