Demonstrated: `git log --format='%H' | while read h; do ...grep -c 'Claude Opus 4.8'...; done | wc -l` = 66 commits carry the hardcoded string; `git log -60 --format=%B | grep -i 'Co-Authored-By: Claude' | sort | uniq -c` = 55 x 'Claude Opus 5', 5 x 'Claude Opus 4.8'. The decisive same-day pair: on 2026-08-04, commits made directly by Claude Code (686c515, 154d8fc, a8653ef) all carry 'Claude Opus 5' while the sv-script commit that day (9396c43) carries 'Claude Opus 4.8'; today's sv commit 624b39a carries 4.8 while the running model is Opus 5. This is the project's own named failure class, in the resource that writes the permanent record: 624b39a — the commit the string is stamped on — is itself a PROVENANCE CORRECTION stating that 'a result attributed to a model that never produced it is, downstream, indistinguishable from a fabricated one', and the standing rule it records forbids exactly this for labels, log directories, report fields, notes and commit messages. Fix: read the model identity at runtime or drop the trailer; do not hardcode a version string in a script that signs commits.

SILENT TRUNCATION: generate_current_state (cdsfl_sv.py, `for f in gs['uncommitted'][:15]`) caps the 'Uncommitted files:' list at 15 entries with no ellipsis, no count and no marker that truncation occurred, so a longer list renders as a complete one. Demonstrated on the pure function with no writes: `python3 -c "...generate_current_state(gs_with_20_uncommitted, 100, None, Path('.'))"` -> 'input files: 20   lines rendered: 15', and the rendered block ends at `- \`M f15.py\`` with nothing indicating five more exist. Currently LATENT — sweeping the last 14 committed CURRENT_STATE.md versions, the highest count observed is 13 (a3d01a7), so the cap has not yet fired. It compounds SV-01: that list is already the contents of the pending commit, and once it exceeds 15 the snapshot understates the commit while looking authoritative. Fix: append a '... and N more' line when the list is truncated.

SILENT NO-OP: `python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py --dry-run --push` exits 0 printing 'State save complete.' having committed and pushed nothing, and prints no indication that the push was skipped. Reproduced: the run's tail shows the normal summary block and rc=0, `git status --short` unchanged, HEAD still 624b39a. The cause is the interaction of two guards — `if args.push: args.commit = True` (line 713-714) forces commit True, then `if args.commit and not args.dry_run` (line 810) skips the commit entirely, and the `elif not args.commit` fallback that would have printed the 'TIP: Use --commit --push' hint is also skipped because commit is now True. So the one flag combination that most looks like a real save is the one that produces the quietest no-op. Fix: if args.dry_run and args.push (or args.commit), print an explicit 'DRY RUN — no commit, no push' line, or reject the combination.

report.headline: Three of the five scripts carry proven defects of the exact shape this project names as its most expensive — most seriously, the log-seal verifier at cdsfl_seal_logs.py:150 discards the boolean half of verify_chain()'s (bool, str) return and therefore prints "OK" for a chain whose own verification returns False, which is then reported by qc as "All log seals verify (Merkle chains intact)".

findings.title: Log-seal verifier can never report TAMPERED — truthiness of a (bool, str) tuple, feeding a green light into qc
findings.evidence:
bench/verification_chain.py:504-506 declares `def verify_chain(self, verifier=None) -> tuple[bool, str]`. scripts/cdsfl_seal_logs.py:150 does `ok = chain.verify_chain()` then `print(f"  {rel}: {'OK' if ok else 'TAMPERED'}")` and `return bool(ok)`.

Command:
  python3 - <<'PY'
  import sys; from pathlib import Path
  sys.path.insert(0,'.'); sys.path.insert(0,'scripts')
  from bench.verification_chain import VerificationChain
  import cdsfl_seal_logs as sl
  bad = VerificationChain.load_json('logs/chat/sealed_chain.json')
  bad._records[0]['entry_hash'] = '0'*64
  res = bad.verify_chain()
  print("TAMPERED chain -> verify_chain() =", (res[0], res[1][:80]))
  print("bool(that tuple) =", bool(res))
  orig = VerificationChain.load_json
  sl.VerificationChain.load_json = staticmethod(lambda p: bad)
  out = sl._verify_dir(Path('logs/chat').resolve())
  sl.VerificationChain.load_json = orig
  print("_verify_dir() returned:", out)
  PY

Real output:
  TAMPERED chain -> verify_chain() = (False, 'Record 0: entry_hash mismatch: stored 000000000000000000000000000000000000000000')
  bool(that tuple) = True

    chat: OK
  _verify_dir() returned: True   <-- True means 'seal OK'

And the green light this produces, from `python3 scripts/cdsfl_seal_logs.py --verify`:
  Verifying 2 sealed directories.
    confer/baseline_confer_run5_20260401: OK
    chat: OK

which cdsfl_qc.py:232-237 converts to:
  OK | logs/ | All log seals verify (Merkle chains intact)

Every other call site in the repo unpacks correctly. `grep -rn "verify_chain()" --include="*.py" . | grep -v __pycache__` returns 26 call sites; 25 are of the form `valid, msg = chain.verify_chain()` (bench/run_round_robin.py:4121, bench/verification_chain.py:827,843, and 22 in bench/tests/). scripts/cdsfl_seal_logs.py:150 is the sole exception.

Age: `git log --format='%h %ci %s' -- scripts/cdsfl_seal_logs.py` shows a single commit, 2c966ca 2026-04-20 04:46:46 +0100. `git log --format='%h %ci' -S"def verify_chain" -- bench/verification_chain.py` gives cb112c6 2026-03-28, i.e. the tuple return predates the script. The defect has been present since the file's first commit — 107 days.

The library itself is sound: `python3 -m pytest bench/tests/test_verification_chain.py -q` -> `98 passed in 0.29s`. There are zero tests for scripts/cdsfl_seal_logs.py (`grep -rln "cdsfl_seal_logs" bench/tests/` returns nothing).
findings.root_cause: A non-empty tuple is always truthy in Python. `verify_chain()` returns `(False, "Record 0: entry_hash mismatch...")` on tamper; `bool((False, "..."))` is `True`. The boolean half of the verdict is discarded before it is ever read. This is structurally identical to the project's own catalogued verdict-reader failure where `NOT FALSIFIED` matched as `FALSIFIED`.
findings.consequence: The tamper-evidence layer's detection branch is dead. A modified sealed log under logs/confer/ or logs/chat/ produces `OK`, cdsfl_seal_logs.py exits 0, and cdsfl_qc.py reports `All log seals verify (Merkle chains intact)`. In a project that documents tamper-evident provenance as a core property, the instrument that would demonstrate it cannot return a negative. The UNSEALED branch (line 145-147) and the ERROR branch (line 153-155) still work, so the failure is confined to — and total within — the TAMPERED case, which is the only case the seal exists for.
findings.proposed_fix: At scripts/cdsfl_seal_logs.py:150 replace `ok = chain.verify_chain()` with `ok, msg = chain.verify_chain()` and include `msg` in the failure print so the diagnostic reaches qc's `bad_lines` filter (cdsfl_qc.py:240-243 already greps for TAMPERED/UNSEALED/ERROR). Add a regression test that seals a temp directory, mutates a byte of a sealed file's recorded hash, and asserts `_verify_dir` returns False — the absence of any test for this file is what let it stand for 107 days.
findings.effort: One line plus one test; under 30 minutes.

findings.title: cdsfl_utils.source_env() does not strip the `export ` prefix, so cdsfl_onboard.py reports all six API keys MISSING — including three marked Required — while they are present; the 2026-07-08 parser incident, repeated in a second script
findings.evidence:
Two scripts in the same directory, run within seconds of each other against the same .env, give opposite verdicts.

  $ python3 scripts/check_model_keys.py
  Credential preflight — /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/.env + environment (values never shown)
    [PRESENT] OPENROUTER_API_KEY  (REQUIRED: Codex + ChatGPT + Gemini panel routes (OpenRouter))
    [PRESENT] DEEPSEEK_API_KEY  (REQUIRED: DeepSeek direct route)
    [PRESENT] GEMINI_API_KEY  (optional: legacy direct-Google fallback ...)
    [PRESENT] GOOGLE_API_KEY  (optional: ...)
    [PRESENT] SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY  (optional: ...)
  OK: all required model-route credentials present.
  EXIT=0

  $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py --full < /dev/null   (API KEYS section, lines 91-103 of captured output)
    !![MISSING] OPENROUTER_API_KEY (Required)
    !![MISSING] GEMINI_API_KEY (Required)
    !![MISSING] DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (Required)
      [MISSING] GOOGLE_API_KEY (Optional)
      [MISSING] OPENAI_API_KEY (Optional)
      [MISSING] GITHUB_TOKEN (Optional)

Mechanism proved directly:
  $ python3 - <<'PY'
  import os, sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts')
  print("BEFORE:", sorted({k for k in os.environ if 'API_KEY' in k or k=='GITHUB_TOKEN'}))
  from cdsfl_utils import source_env; source_env()
  print("AFTER:", sorted({k for k in os.environ if 'API_KEY' in k or 'GITHUB_TOKEN' in k}))
  print("get('OPENROUTER_API_KEY') is None ->", os.environ.get('OPENROUTER_API_KEY') is None)
  print("get('export OPENROUTER_API_KEY') is None ->", os.environ.get('export OPENROUTER_API_KEY') is None)
  PY
  BEFORE: []
  AFTER: ['SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY', 'export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY', 'export GEMINI_API_KEY', 'export GITHUB_TOKEN', 'export GOOGLE_API_KEY', 'export GROQ_API_KEY', 'export MOONSHOT_API_KEY', 'export OPENAI_API_KEY', 'export OPENROUTER_API_KEY']
  get('OPENROUTER_API_KEY') is None -> True
  get('export OPENROUTER_API_KEY') is None -> False

.env key names (values never read or printed) confirm eight of nine entries carry the `export ` prefix; SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY does not, and it is the only name source_env() sets correctly.

The docstring at cdsfl_utils.py:356 claims this function "mirrors runner_core.py". It does not. bench/runner_core.py:164-174:
    if line.startswith("export "):
        line = line[7:]
    key, _, val = line.partition("=")
The runner strips the prefix. cdsfl_utils.py:364-368 does not.

Security check requested by the brief, run and clean: scanning all three captured script outputs against every value in .env, including 8-character tails, returned `LEAKS FOUND: NONE` across 9 secrets. No key value is printed by any script.
findings.root_cause: cdsfl_utils.source_env() (lines 360-368) partitions each .env line on `=` without first removing a leading `export `, producing environment variable names literally called `export OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. cdsfl_onboard.check_api_keys() then queries `os.environ.get("OPENROUTER_API_KEY")` and gets None. This is the same parser defect recorded in persistent memory for 2026-07-08, which manufactured a false "keys were destroyed" incident; it was fixed in check_model_keys.py (which documents the lesson in its own source at lines 33-38) and left unfixed in cdsfl_utils.py.
findings.consequence: The script memory designates as "a researcher's first contact with the project" tells that researcher three Required credentials are absent when they are present, and offers no route to discover otherwise. The two scripts contradict each other on the same fact. The project has already paid for this exact false negative once; the fix landed in one of the two parsers only. Any future consumer of cdsfl_utils.source_env() inherits the same false negative silently — nothing errors, keys simply appear to be missing.
findings.proposed_fix:
In cdsfl_utils.py source_env(), insert the runner's two lines before the partition:
    if line.startswith("export "):
        line = line[len("export "):].lstrip()
Better: delete cdsfl_utils.source_env() entirely and import bench.runner_core.source_env, so the "mirrors runner_core.py" claim becomes structurally true rather than a comment that drifted. Add a test asserting an export-prefixed line yields the bare key name — the same test check_model_keys.py should also carry.
findings.effort: Two lines, or one import plus deletion; under 30 minutes including the test.

findings.title: `qc` has not completed a run since 2026-04-22 — cdsfl_qc.py dies with an unhandled OSError before printing any findings, and three of its seven checks never execute
findings.evidence:
$ python3 scripts/cdsfl_qc.py
  CDSFL Quality Control — 2026-08-05T14:30:57+01:00
  Repository: /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering
  ======================================================================

  Checking timestamps...
  Checking test consistency...
  Checking experiment consistency...
  Checking file references...
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File ".../scripts/cdsfl_qc.py", line 373, in <module>
      main()
    File ".../scripts/cdsfl_qc.py", line 337, in main

    File ".../scripts/cdsfl_qc.py", line 153, in check_broken_references
      broken = check_file_references(md)
    File ".../scripts/cdsfl_utils.py", line 338, in check_file_references
      if not (from_file.exists() or from_root.exists()
  OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long: ".../experimental_notes/ to the consolidated plan (repo + Desktop mirror, byte-identical post-edit) immediately after §6a's post-launch path paragraph. ..."

  $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_qc.py > qc_out.txt 2>&1; echo "REAL_EXIT=$?"
  REAL_EXIT=1
  27 lines of output, none of them a FINDINGS block.

Four crash-capable references identified (max path component in bytes; macOS NAME_MAX is 255):
  experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md line 343 maxcomp 386
  experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md line 363 maxcomp 319
  experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md line 389 maxcomp 266
  experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md line 395 maxcomp 261

Age, established by replaying every revision of that file through the reference checker: the first version of experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md, commit 991cde0 2026-04-22 02:10:20 +0100, already carries maxcomp=386, and every one of the 54 subsequent revisions through 9396c43 2026-08-04 does too. Re-run with the *historical* heuristic in force at that date (`_is_likely_not_a_path` from commit 491b08d, 2026-04-11) against the file at 991cde0: max component bytes = 386, crash-capable refs = 2. The crash is not an artefact of the currently-modified working copy — it reproduces from committed content at every point in the file's history.

That is 105 days during which the `qc` command could not complete.

The three checks that never run: check_glossary (cdsfl_qc.py:339), check_onboard_script (:342), check_log_seals (:345). Executing them by hand shows they would have produced output — 58 glossary terms, an onboard dry-run verdict, and a seal verdict.

Zero tests cover this: `grep -rln "cdsfl_qc\|cdsfl_utils\|cdsfl_onboard\|cdsfl_sv\|cdsfl_recover" bench/tests/` returns only bench/tests/test_sv_commit.py.
findings.root_cause: check_file_references (cdsfl_utils.py:306-352) extracts backtick-delimited spans with `` r"`([^`]+/[^`]+)`" `` and treats each as a candidate path. Prose containing an unbalanced backtick yields a several-hundred-character 'reference'. The `_is_likely_not_a_path` heuristic (lines 242-303) has no length guard, so the string reaches `Path.exists()`, which raises OSError ENAMETOOLONG when any single path component exceeds 255 bytes. The `try/except OSError` at lines 309-312 wraps only `read_text`, not the three `.exists()` calls at lines 338-339.
findings.consequence: The founder's `qc` command, specified in .claude/CLAUDE.md as "run `python3 scripts/cdsfl_qc.py` and fix reported issues", has produced no findings report for 105 days. It fails loudly, which is the one merciful part — but the practical effect is that the repo has had no automated staleness sweep across the entire Exp 40-54 arc, which is precisely the window in which docs-defect-parity matters most.
findings.proposed_fix: Two independent guards, both needed. (1) In `_is_likely_not_a_path`, reject any ref whose longest `/`-separated component exceeds 255 bytes, or more simply any ref longer than ~200 characters — no real path in this repo approaches that. (2) Wrap the three `.exists()` calls at cdsfl_utils.py:338-345 in `try/except OSError` and treat an OSError as 'not a path' rather than propagating. Guard (2) alone stops the crash; guard (1) alone stops the false candidates; do both, because (2) is the one that keeps a future malformed markdown line from taking the whole tool down again.
findings.effort: Roughly 10 lines across two functions, plus a test fixture containing an over-long backtick span; 1 hour.

findings.title: cdsfl_onboard.py --full is a byte-for-byte no-op, and --dry-run, the self-test that exists to catch exactly this, reports OK — the feature has never worked since it was created 118 days ago
findings.evidence:
$ python3 scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py < /dev/null > onb_def.txt 2>&1
  $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py --full < /dev/null > onb_full.txt 2>&1
  $ diff onb_def.txt onb_full.txt; echo "DIFF_EXIT=$?"
  DIFF_EXIT=0        (227 identical lines; --full adds nothing)

--help promises otherwise:
  --full      Include the SV:LATEST_EXP block in the project summary (full
              ONBOARDING state).

Mechanism proved:
  $ python3 - <<'PY'
  import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts')
  import cdsfl_onboard as ob
  from cdsfl_utils import repo_root, read_section
  root = repo_root()
  sec = read_section(root/'resources'/'ONBOARDING.md', "## What This Project Is", "\n## ")
  print("extracted section length:", len(sec))
  print("SV_START in extracted section:", ob.SV_START_MARKER in sec)
  a = ob.read_onboarding_what_is(root, strip_sv=True)
  b = ob.read_onboarding_what_is(root, strip_sv=False)
  print("default == full summary text:", a == b, "| len", len(a), len(b))
  full_txt = (root/'resources'/'ONBOARDING.md').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
  print("markers exist somewhere in file (what dry_run checks):", ob.SV_START_MARKER in full_txt, ob.SV_END_MARKER in full_txt)
  print("dry_run() exit code:", ob.dry_run(root))
  PY
  extracted section length: 884
  SV_START in extracted section: False
  SV_END   in extracted section: False
  default == full summary text: True | len 884 884
  markers exist somewhere in file (what dry_run checks): True True
  cdsfl_onboard --dry-run: OK
  dry_run() exit code: 0

File layout confirms it: `grep -n "^## " resources/ONBOARDING.md` gives `8:## What This Project Is`, `25:## Standing Rules...`, `93:## Current State...`. `grep -n "SV:LATEST_EXP_START" resources/ONBOARDING.md` gives line 95, and the END marker line 1061. The markers live inside `## Current State`, 70 lines below the end of the section --full reads.

Age: replaying all 188 revisions of resources/ONBOARDING.md and testing marker position against the extracted section at each one gives exactly two state changes — markers absent until f528314 2026-04-09 18:16:35 +0100 ("Enhance sv script: auto-update ONBOARDING.md and RECOVERY.md"), then OUT-OF-SECTION from that commit onward, permanently. The markers were never once inside the section --full reads. The feature has not worked on any day of its 118-day existence.
findings.root_cause: read_onboarding_what_is (cdsfl_onboard.py:341-356) extracts only the `## What This Project Is` section, then searches that extract for the SV markers. cdsfl_sv.py writes those markers into the `## Current State` section instead. `content.find(SV_START_MARKER)` returns -1, the `if start != -1 and end != -1` guard at line 354 silently declines to strip, and strip_sv=True and strip_sv=False converge on identical output. dry_run() (lines 459-481) validates that the markers exist *anywhere in the file* (line 463-466) rather than that they fall within the section the reader actually consumes, so the self-test cannot observe the divergence it was written to guard.
findings.consequence: Two distinct harms. First, --full silently delivers the default view, so anyone using onboard as the documented "dynamic information source" to get full ONBOARDING state gets a 884-character stub and no indication anything is missing. Second and worse, cdsfl_qc.py:297-302 consumes the dry-run's exit 0 and reports `OK | scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py | --dry-run passes (canonical-doc wiring intact)`. The wiring is not intact. A self-test that certifies a feature which has never functioned is the precise failure shape this project names as its most expensive kind.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide which section owns the SV block and make reader, writer and self-test agree. Least disruptive: change read_onboarding_what_is to read the SV block from wherever the markers actually are (search the whole file for the marker pair and splice) rather than from within one section. Then harden dry_run to assert the property that matters — `SV_START_MARKER in read_section(onboarding, "## What This Project Is", "\n## ")` if the section-scoped design is kept, or `read_onboarding_what_is(root, strip_sv=False) != read_onboarding_what_is(root, strip_sv=True)` if not. The second form is the better test because it asserts the observable behaviour --full promises rather than a proxy for it.
findings.effort: Half a day, because it requires a ruling on which document section owns the block and a matching check in cdsfl_sv.py's writer.

findings.title: cdsfl_utils.latest_experiment() returns None whenever the highest-numbered experiment lacks a report file — so the `rs` recovery script states "(No experiment logs found)" with 68 experiment directories and 37 reports on disk
findings.evidence:
$ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py 2>&1 | grep -n "LATEST EXPERIMENT" -A 3
  85:## LATEST EXPERIMENT
  86-
  87-  (No experiment logs found)

Against reality:
  $ ls -d bench/logs/exp*/ | wc -l
        68
  $ ls bench/logs/exp*/exp*_report.json | wc -l
        37

Mechanism:
  $ python3 - <<'PY'  (abridged)
  max exp number: 53
  dirs at max: ['exp53_control_zero_live_20260729T222431Z', 'exp53_control_zero_live_20260801T005649Z']
  reports at max: [[], []]
  first lower-numbered exp WITH a report: 49 exp49_engineering_exam_live_20260729T062320Z
  PY

  $ python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from cdsfl_utils import latest_experiment; print(latest_experiment())"
  None

Downstream, all three consumers degrade silently rather than loudly:
  - scripts/cdsfl_recover.py:96-97 prints the false "(No experiment logs found)".
  - scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py:384-389 has `if exp:` with no else branch, so the entire 'Latest experiment' block vanishes from the summary. Confirmed absent from all 227 lines of onboard --full output.
  - scripts/cdsfl_qc.py:115-117 returns an empty finding list immediately, so the documented check 4 'Experiment number consistency between docs and logs' silently performs no check.

Dating: the two exp53 directories are the only exp53 entries and both lack a report; their timestamps are 20260729T222431Z and 20260801T005649Z. The defect therefore activated on 2026-07-29, when the first report-less exp53 directory appeared — approximately 7 days.

A secondary latent defect sits behind it: cdsfl_qc.py:126 scans ONBOARDING.md with `re.finditer(r"EXP\s+(\d+)", text)`, uppercase only. Measured: the highest uppercase 'EXP N' in ONBOARDING.md is 42, while the highest mixed-case 'Exp N' is 54. If latest_experiment() were repaired without also fixing this regex, the check would begin emitting a STALE finding against a document that is not stale.
findings.root_cause: latest_experiment (cdsfl_utils.py:112-213) takes `max_n = max(n for n, _ in exp_dirs)` at line 133 and then only ever considers directories at that single number (line 135). If none of them contains an `exp*_report.json`, the loop at line 140 exhausts via `continue` and the function falls through to `return None` at line 213. There is no fallback to the next-highest experiment that does have a report, and no distinction between 'no logs exist' and 'the newest log has no report yet'. Runs that are checkpointed but never produce a report — control runs, aborted runs — therefore blind the function to the entire history behind them.
findings.consequence: A recovery resource reports something false. `rs` is specified in .claude/CLAUDE.md as "run `python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py --full` and rebuild context from output", and after a context compaction that output is a primary input. An agent or a founder rebuilding state is told there are no experiment logs at all, when exp49 carries a complete parseable report. This is worse than a crash, because the sentence reads like a fact about the project rather than a fault in the tool.
findings.proposed_fix: In latest_experiment, iterate experiment numbers in descending order and return the first that yields a parseable report, rather than binding to max_n only. Where the highest-numbered experiment is skipped for lack of a report, say so in the returned dict (e.g. a `newer_without_report` field) so recover can print 'latest with report: exp49; exp53 present but unreported' instead of silently reporting the older one as newest. Separately, give cdsfl_recover.py:96-97 and cdsfl_onboard.py:384 a distinguishable message for 'no logs directory' versus 'logs exist but none parseable' — the current single message conflates a healthy empty repo with a broken parser. Fix the uppercase-only `EXP\s+` regex at cdsfl_qc.py:126 to `[Ee]xp\s+` in the same change, or repairing this finding will produce a false STALE finding.
findings.effort: 2-3 hours including the qc regex fix and a fixture with a report-less newest directory.

findings.title: qc's test-count check is a silent no-op — it matches a phrasing RECOVERY.md does not use, so it reports nothing at all while a 454-test drift stands
findings.evidence:
Running each qc check in isolation (bypassing the F3 crash):
  === check_test_consistency -> 0 findings

Not a WARN, not an OK — zero output of any kind.

Why:
  $ python3 - <<'PY'
  import sys, re; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts')
  from cdsfl_utils import test_count, repo_root
  root = repo_root()
  print("test_count() ->", test_count())
  rec = (root/'resources'/'RECOVERY.md').read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines()
  sec = "\n".join(rec[:100])
  print("regex matches in first 100 lines:", re.findall(r"(\d+)\s+tests?\s+pass", sec))
  PY
  test_count() -> 2556
  regex matches in first 100 lines: []

The drift the check exists to catch is real and present. RECOVERY.md's current-state section, lines 33-34, records:
  "-> 2099 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed in 123 s; 49 outbound attempts, all denied (2102 collected). Re-measured 20:45 BST after the earlier 19:15 figure went..."

Independently confirmed current figure:
  $ python3 -m pytest bench/tests/ --co -q | tail -3
  2556 tests collected in 7.07s

So the documented figure is 2102 collected and the actual figure is 2556 — a 454-test gap — and check_test_consistency emits nothing.

Two further checks in the same file are similarly unable to fail:
  - check_staleness (cdsfl_qc.py:36-68) emits only category "INFO" and "MISSING". It prints the doc timestamp beside the last commit date and compares nothing, despite the module docstring at line 9 listing check 1 as "Stale documentation (timestamps older than last commit)". Live output: `INFO | resources/ONBOARDING.md | Doc timestamp: 5 August 2026 14:08 BST | Last commit: 2026-08-05 14:08:53 +0100`. There is no code path by which it can produce a STALE finding.
  - The documented `--fix-timestamps` flag does not exist. cdsfl_qc.py:4-6 states "Usage: python3 scripts/cdsfl_qc.py [--fix-timestamps] / --fix-timestamps Update stale timestamps (otherwise report only)", but main() at line 317-318 calls `parser.parse_args()` having added no arguments:
      $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_qc.py --fix-timestamps
      usage: cdsfl_qc.py [-h]
      cdsfl_qc.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --fix-timestamps
findings.root_cause: check_test_consistency (cdsfl_qc.py:91) searches for `r"(\d+)\s+tests?\s+pass"`. RECOVERY.md writes pass counts as "2099 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed" and collection counts as "(2102 collected)". Neither form matches. When `matches` is empty the function returns an empty list — there is no else branch reporting that the check found nothing to check, so a failure to locate the subject is indistinguishable from a clean result. check_staleness has the same defect in a different form: it gathers the two dates and never compares them.
findings.consequence: Once the F3 crash is repaired, qc will print `Total: N checks, 0 issues (0 stale, 0 broken refs, 0 missing, 0 warnings)` while RECOVERY.md's headline test figure is 454 tests out of date and no timestamp comparison has occurred. That is a clean bill of health issued over a stale repo, which is worse than no qc tool at all, because the founder's documented workflow is to run qc and fix what it reports. Three of the five checks the module docstring advertises — staleness, test-count consistency, and experiment consistency (see F5) — currently cannot produce a finding.
findings.proposed_fix: For the test count: match the phrasing that actually appears, e.g. `r"(\d+)\s+(?:tests?\s+)?(?:collected|passed)"`, and emit a WARN when the regex finds no candidate at all so a phrasing change surfaces as an issue instead of as silence. For staleness: parse both dates and emit STALE when the doc timestamp precedes the last commit by more than a threshold, which is what the docstring already promises. For `--fix-timestamps`: either implement it or delete the two lines of usage text at cdsfl_qc.py:4-6 — a documented flag that argparse rejects is a claim the tool cannot honour. As a general guard, make every check emit at least one finding of some category on every run, so 'checked and clean' is visibly distinct from 'did not check'.
findings.effort: 3-4 hours for all three, most of it deciding the staleness threshold.

             Gemini 3.1 Pro dispatch via Google GenAI API
    !![MISSING] DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (Required)

check_model_keys.py, lines 23-27, classifies the same key differently:

And its live output confirms:

The project's own panel record (.claude/CLAUDE.md, Model Confer Dispatch) states Gemini "moved from direct Google API to OpenRouter on 2026-05-10", and for DeepSeek: "upgraded from R1-0528 on 2026-05-10; the older `deepseek-reasoner` is no longer listed by DeepSeek". The current identifier is `deepseek-v4-pro`.

So cdsfl_onboard.py:83 names a model DeepSeek no longer lists, and cdsfl_onboard.py:82 marks as Required a key the panel stopped routing through 87 days ago. The Gemini description also names the wrong transport (Google GenAI API rather than OpenRouter).

Note what is NOT wrong: WOLFRAM_API_KEY does not appear in cdsfl_onboard.py's API_KEYS dict at all, nor in check_model_keys.py. The 2026-08-03 removal left no dead key reference in either script. `grep -rn "WOLFRAM_API_KEY" .env` returns only the archival comment.
findings.root_cause: The API_KEYS dict at cdsfl_onboard.py:80-87 is hardcoded and was not revisited when the panel rotated on 2026-05-10, whereas check_model_keys.py was written afterwards (2026-07-06) against the then-current panel. The two scripts hold independent copies of the same fact and have drifted apart.
findings.consequence: Onboarding a new researcher, or an agent reading onboard as the documented information source, produces a wrong picture of the live panel: an optional legacy fallback flagged as Required with `!!`, a retired model named as the active one, and the wrong transport for Gemini. Contradiction between two scripts in the same directory means whichever is read second has to be adjudicated by hand. Severity is LOW only because the contradiction is currently masked by F2 — both keys read as MISSING regardless — but repairing F2 makes this the visible surface.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the API_KEYS dict from cdsfl_onboard.py and have check_api_keys() import REQUIRED and OPTIONAL from check_model_keys, so there is one definition of which credentials the panel needs. findings.title: cdsfl_onboard.py reports [FOUND] for the Wolfram MCP Bridge, which the project retired on 2026-08-03, and does not check the route that replaced it
findings.evidence:
Live output from the `--full` run, SYSTEM TOOLS section:
    Wolfram MCP Bridge:
      [FOUND] Wolfram Local MCP Bridge

The check at cdsfl_onboard.py:264 tests only `Path("/Applications/WolframLocalMCPBridge.app").exists()`, and the stale app bundle is still on disk:
  $ ls -d /Applications/WolframLocalMCPBridge.app
  /Applications/WolframLocalMCPBridge.app

The project's own record says that component is dead. `grep -n '^#' .env` lines 12-15:
  # WOLFRAM_API_KEY removed 2026-08-03: Wolfram retired the MCP Service and the key
  # stopped functioning after 2026-07-31. Nothing in the codebase ever read it.
  # Archived (not deleted) at ~/CDSFL_retired_credentials/. Wolfram now needs no
  # credential: WolframCloud MCP + local Engine via wolframscript.

.claude/CLAUDE.md, section "HOW WOLFRAM IS WIRED (settled 2026-08-02)", names the two live routes: the WolframCloud MCP server via `npx -y mcp-remote https://agenttools.wolfram.com/mcp`, and the local Engine invoked on demand through wolframscript.

The live route is installed and unchecked:
  $ which wolframscript
  /usr/local/bin/wolframscript

Relatedly, cdsfl_onboard.py:75 still lists the `wolframalpha` pip package under OPTIONAL_PACKAGES as "Wolfram Alpha API client" and reports it [FOUND] — a client for the key-authenticated API whose credential was archived on 2026-08-03.
findings.root_cause: check_wolfram_mcp() infers a capability from the presence of an application bundle. The bundle outlived the service it talked to: Wolfram retired the MCP Service and the key stopped working after 2026-07-31, but nothing removed the .app from /Applications. Existence on disk is not the same property as being able to function, and the check conflates them.
findings.consequence: The dynamic information source reports a green [FOUND] for infrastructure that cannot work, and stays silent about wolframscript, which is what actually runs. A researcher told the bridge is present will reach for it and hit the failure mode .claude/CLAUDE.md specifically warns about — a Wolfram call that returns an error string shaped like an answer. Severity is LOW because the consequence is a wasted detour rather than a corrupted result, but it is the same green-light-over-dead-component shape as F1 and F4, and it is a check that can only ever say FOUND once the bundle exists.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace check_wolfram_mcp() with a check for the two live routes: `shutil.which("wolframscript")` for the local Engine, and `shutil.which("npx")` for the WolframCloud MCP shim. If /Applications/WolframLocalMCPBridge.app is still present, report it explicitly as RETIRED with the 2026-08-03 date rather than as FOUND, so the stale bundle produces a prompt to remove it instead of false reassurance. Drop `wolframalpha` from OPTIONAL_PACKAGES, or re-label it so it is not read as an active dependency. Worth adding: .claude/CLAUDE.md records $LicenseExpirationDate 2026-09-11 for the local Engine, five weeks out — an onboarding check that surfaces that date would earn its place where the current one does not.
findings.effort: 1 hour.

findings.evidence:

  test_sv_commit.py

Of the five scripts in this audit — cdsfl_qc.py, cdsfl_onboard.py, check_model_keys.py, cdsfl_seal_logs.py, cdsfl_utils.py — exactly zero appear in any test. The only operational script with tests is cdsfl_sv.py, which is outside this audit's scope.

The suite is otherwise healthy and large: `python3 -m pytest bench/tests/ --co -q` collects 2556 tests, and the library underneath the broken seal verifier passes cleanly (`python3 -m pytest bench/tests/test_verification_chain.py -q` -> 98 passed in 0.29s). The coverage gap is specific to scripts/, not general.

Measured cost of the gap, from the findings above: F3 ran undetected for 105 days, F1 for 107 days, F4 for 118 days — the whole of its existence.
findings.root_cause: scripts/ was treated as automation rather than as code, so it was never brought under the test discipline that bench/ operates under. Every defect in this report is mechanically detectable by a test of under ten lines: F1 by sealing a fixture and corrupting it, F2 by asserting an export-prefixed line yields a bare key name, F3 by running the reference checker over a markdown fixture with an over-long backtick span, F4 by asserting --full and default differ, F5 by pointing latest_experiment at a fixture whose newest directory has no report, F6 by asserting each check emits at least one finding.
findings.consequence: The scripts that report on the project's health are the least verified code in the project. That inverts the intended reliability gradient: the instruments are less trustworthy than what they measure, and their failures are reported as clean results. This is the ruling the founder should make, because it is a scope decision rather than a bug — whether scripts/ comes under bench/tests/ discipline, and at what point in the Exp 40-54 arc that work is scheduled.
findings.proposed_fix: Add bench/tests/test_operational_scripts.py covering the six behaviours listed above. Each is a small fixture-driven test; together they would have caught every finding in this report. Recommend scheduling against a concrete trigger rather than deferring: the natural one is the same window in which F1 and F2 are fixed, since both fixes need a regression test anyway and the file will already exist.

verdicts.title: Log-seal verifier can never report TAMPERED — truthiness of a (bool, str) tuple
verdicts.reproduction:
I reproduced the mechanism WITHOUT using the auditor's load_json substitution, so the result does not depend on their harness. Command:

  python3 - <<'PY'
  import sys; from pathlib import Path
  sys.path.insert(0,'.'); sys.path.insert(0,'scripts')
  from bench.verification_chain import VerificationChain
  import cdsfl_seal_logs as sl
  orig = VerificationChain._verify_single
  VerificationChain._verify_single = lambda self,i,rec,verifier=None: (False,"SIMULATED entry_hash mismatch")
  try:
      c = VerificationChain.load_json('logs/chat/sealed_chain.json')
      print("verify_chain() now ->", c.verify_chain())
      print("_verify_dir() ->", sl._verify_dir(Path('logs/chat').resolve()))
  finally:
      VerificationChain._verify_single = orig
  PY

Output:
  verify_chain() now -> (False, 'Record 0: SIMULATED entry_hash mismatch')
    chat: OK
  _verify_dir() -> True

So the real on-disk chain, made to fail verification at the library level, still prints OK and returns True. Also confirmed directly: bool((False, '...')) is True. `python3 scripts/cdsfl_seal_logs.py --verify` -> 'chat: OK', EXIT=0. And running the qc check in isolation, `Q.check_log_seals(root)` -> [{'category': 'OK', 'file': 'logs/', 'detail': 'All log seals verify (Merkle chains intact)'}] — the exact green light claimed.

Call-site survey: `grep -rn "verify_chain()" --include="*.py" . | grep -v __pycache__` gives 27 lines; the only two non-unpacking uses are bench/run_round_robin.py:275, which is a correctly-typed `-> tuple[bool, str]` pass-through wrapper (not a defect), and scripts/cdsfl_seal_logs.py:150. Age verified: `git log --format='%h %ci %s' -- scripts/cdsfl_seal_logs.py` -> single commit 2c966ca 2026-04-20 04:46:46 +0100; `git log -S"def verify_chain" -- bench/verification_chain.py | tail` -> cb112c6 2026-03-28. `grep -rln "cdsfl_seal_logs" bench/tests/` -> no output.

WHY UNDERSTATED, not CONFIRMED. The stated consequence — 'A modified sealed log under logs/confer/ or logs/chat/ produces OK' — is true, but it has a SECOND, independent cause the auditor did not find, and the proposed fix does not touch it. verify_chain() performs zero file I/O, so it cannot see a modified log file at all:

  python3 - <<'PY'
  import sys, builtins, pathlib
  sys.path.insert(0,'.')
  from bench.verification_chain import VerificationChain
  c = VerificationChain.load_json('logs/chat/sealed_chain.json')
  def boom(*a, **k): raise AssertionError("verify_chain performed file I/O")
  builtins.open = boom; pathlib.Path.read_text = boom
  print(c.verify_chain())
  PY
  -> (True, 'All 1 records verified.')

With every file read blocked, verification still passes. Compounding it, the records are written with storage_mode="hash_only" (confirmed in logs/chat/sealed_chain.json), and bench/verification_chain.py:727 gates the payload_hash comparison on `if sealed_body["storage_mode"] == "full_payload"` — so even the stored hash is never re-checked. I recomputed the leaf by hand: current logs/chat/README.md hashes to sha256:e4e19a99…f278ff, matching the stored payload_hash exactly; a one-byte addition gives sha256:990dfc2a…4126b. Nothing in the verify path ever performs that comparison.

Consequence for the fix: `ok, msg = chain.verify_chain()` restores detection of tampering with sealed_chain.json ITSELF, and nothing else. The module docstring at scripts/cdsfl_seal_logs.py:16-18 promises 'any modification to a sealed file invalidates the Merkle root' and --help promises 'exit non-zero on tamper'. After the proposed repair, editing a sealed log file still yields OK and exit 0. Applying only the tuple fix and calling the seal layer repaired would be the project's own catalogued failure shape a second time: a green light restored over a hole that is still open.

verdicts.title: cdsfl_utils.source_env() does not strip the `export ` prefix, so onboard reports all six keys MISSING
verdicts.reproduction:
Reproduced in a scrubbed environment so no inherited shell variable could mask it:

  env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/bin python3 - <<'PY'
  import os, sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts')
  from cdsfl_utils import source_env; source_env()
  for k in sorted(k for k in os.environ if 'API_KEY' in k or 'TOKEN' in k): print(repr(k))
  print(os.environ.get('OPENROUTER_API_KEY'))
  PY

Output: names created are 'SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY', 'export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY', 'export GEMINI_API_KEY', 'export GITHUB_TOKEN', 'export GOOGLE_API_KEY', 'export GROQ_API_KEY', 'export MOONSHOT_API_KEY', 'export OPENAI_API_KEY', 'export OPENROUTER_API_KEY'; and os.environ.get('OPENROUTER_API_KEY') -> None. Eight of nine names carry the literal prefix.

I verified the root cause CAUSALLY rather than by inspection — I substituted a stripping parser and re-ran the same function:

  python3 - <<'PY'
  import sys, os; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts')
  import cdsfl_utils, cdsfl_onboard as ob
  def fixed():
      for line in (cdsfl_utils.repo_root()/'.env').read_text().splitlines():
          line=line.strip()
          if not line or line.startswith('#') or '=' not in line: continue
          if line.startswith('export '): line=line[7:]
          k,_,v=line.partition('='); os.environ.setdefault(k.strip(), v.strip().strip("'\""))
  ob.source_env = fixed
  ob.check_api_keys()
  PY

All six flip from MISSING to [FOUND], including the three Required. Nothing else changed. That isolates cdsfl_utils.source_env() as the sole cause.

Baseline confirmed too: `python3 scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py --full < /dev/null` prints !![MISSING] for OPENROUTER_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (all 'Required') while `python3 scripts/check_model_keys.py` prints [PRESENT] for all five it names, EXIT=0, in the same working tree seconds apart. My agent environment has none of these keys exported (checked: all six report 'unset'), so setdefault is not masking anything. bench/runner_core.py:169-171 does strip the prefix; cdsfl_utils.py:364 does not, despite the docstring 'mirrors runner_core.py'.

Two caveats on the fix, neither of which changes the verdict. (a) Blast radius is exactly one consumer: `grep -n source_env scripts/*.py` shows cdsfl_onboard.py:288 is the only caller, so no experiment path is affected — the runner has its own correct parser. 'BLOCKING' therefore overstates urgency in the project's own severity convention, though the false report in an onboarding resource is real. (b) The auditor's preferred fix, importing bench.runner_core.source_env, is not behaviour-neutral: runner_core uses `os.environ[k] = v` (overwrite) where cdsfl_utils uses setdefault (shell wins), and runner_core does not strip surrounding quotes where cdsfl_utils does `.strip("'\"")`. I checked .env — no value is currently quoted, so nothing breaks today, but a quoted value added later would be passed through with its quotes. The two-line inline strip the auditor lists first is the safer edit.

verdicts.title: qc dies with unhandled OSError before printing findings; three of seven checks never execute
verdicts.reproduction:
`python3 scripts/cdsfl_qc.py` -> OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long, raised at scripts/cdsfl_utils.py:338 `from_file.exists()`, propagating through cdsfl_qc.py:153 -> :337 -> :373. `python3 scripts/cdsfl_qc.py >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?` -> 1. `python3 scripts/cdsfl_qc.py 2>&1 | grep -c FINDINGS` -> 0.

The critical check the auditor's claim rests on is that this is not an artefact of the one dirty file in the tree. I tested COMMITTED content only, via git show, never touching the working copy:

  python3 - <<'PY'  (reimplements the extraction + _is_likely_not_a_path filter, measures max path-component bytes)
  committed = subprocess.run(['git','show','HEAD:experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md'],...)
  PY
  HEAD version crash-capable refs: [(325, 386), (344, 319), (370, 266), (376, 261)]

Repo-wide over every tracked .md at HEAD, exactly one file is crash-capable: experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md. Replaying the file's first revision, `git show 991cde0:...` (991cde0, 2026-04-22 02:10:20 +0100 — confirmed as the first commit touching that path), gives crash-capable refs [(189, 386), (231, 266)] under the CURRENT heuristic. macOS NAME_MAX is 255. `git show 991cde0:scripts/cdsfl_qc.py | grep -n check_broken_references` confirms the checker was already wired at :337 on that date, so 105 days is right.

Check ordering verified at cdsfl_qc.py:327-346: staleness, test consistency, experiment consistency, broken references (crash), then glossary, onboard wiring, log seals — 3 of 7 never reached. Running those three by hand: check_glossary -> INFO '58 terms defined'; check_onboard_script -> OK '--dry-run passes (canonical-doc wiring intact)'; check_log_seals -> OK 'All log seals verify (Merkle chains intact)'. All three produce output, exactly as claimed. Test coverage: `grep -rln "cdsfl_qc|cdsfl_utils|cdsfl_onboard|cdsfl_sv|cdsfl_recover" bench/tests/` -> only bench/tests/test_sv_commit.py, whose imports are `from cdsfl_sv import ...` only.

One thing the auditor did not measure, which bears on whether the fix delivers a working tool. I ran check_broken_references with Path.exists wrapped so OSError returns False — i.e. exactly guard (2) applied — and it completes but emits 236 BROKEN_REF findings: 59 in the Agent Operational Plan, 40 in RECOVERY.md, 28 in the Consolidated Plan, 25 in ONBOARDING.md. Sampled details include 'agenttools.wolfram.com/mcp', 'npx -y mcp-remote https://agenttools.wolfram.com/mcp' and 'bash bench/arc_sequencer.sh' — protocol-less URLs and shell commands the heuristic does not filter. So both proposed guards are correct and necessary, but they restore a check that then buries any real broken reference in ~200 false positives. The fix stops the crash; it does not by itself make qc usable, and shipping it without a heuristic pass would trade a loud failure for a quiet one.

verdicts.title: latest_experiment() returns None when the highest-numbered experiment lacks a report; recover prints '(No experiment logs found)'
verdicts.reproduction:
python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from cdsfl_utils import latest_experiment; print(latest_experiment())" -> None
  python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py 2>&1 | grep -n 'LATEST EXPERIMENT' -A 3 -> line 85 '## LATEST EXPERIMENT', line 87 '  (No experiment logs found)'

With latest_experiment repaired to 49 and the regex left uppercase-only, cdsfl_qc.py:126-131 would compare 42 < 49 and emit a STALE finding against a document that mentions Exp 54. Dating verified: exp dirs >= 48 are exp48 (report present, 2026-07-29), exp49 (report present, 2026-07-29), and the two report-less exp53 dirs (mtimes 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-01, run stamps 20260729T222431Z / 20260801T005649Z). verdicts.title: qc's test-count check is a silent no-op; check_staleness cannot emit STALE; --fix-timestamps is documented but unimplemented
verdicts.reproduction:
All three sub-claims reproduced.
  check_test_consistency(root) -> [] (zero findings of any category). test_count() -> 2556. re.findall(r"(\d+)\s+tests?\s+pass", first_100_lines_of_RECOVERY.md) -> []. The regex has no subject, and cdsfl_qc.py:91-104 has no else branch, so 'found nothing to check' is indistinguishable from 'clean'.
  check_staleness(root) -> two findings, both category INFO: 'Doc timestamp: 5 August 2026 14:08 BST | Last commit: 2026-08-05 14:08:53 +0100' for ONBOARDING.md and RECOVERY.md. Reading cdsfl_qc.py:36-68 confirms the two dates are formatted into a string and never compared; there is no STALE branch, against docstring check 1.
  python3 scripts/cdsfl_qc.py --fix-timestamps -> 'cdsfl_qc.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --fix-timestamps', exit code 2 (measured). cdsfl_qc.py:4-6 documents the flag; main() calls parse_args() having added none.
  Independent count: python3 -m pytest bench/tests/ --co -q | tail -3 -> '2556 tests collected in 3.59s'.

Two corrections that do not change the verdict but change what should be done.

(a) The '454-test drift stands' framing is softer than presented. resources/RECOVERY.md lines 30-42 label the figure 'Current figure, with outbound calls actually denied, `d4d4d7f` plus the working tree, re-measured 2026-07-31 19:15 BST', and the same block warns that 'A pass-count taken against an uncommitted tree is a point-in-time observation, not a reproducible figure' and that public documents should 'defer the number to docs/CURRENT_STATE.md'. It is a dated, commit-anchored measurement, not an unqualified current-state claim. The no-op check is the defect; the doc is closer to correct than the finding implies.

(b) The proposed regex is itself defective and would ship a permanent false positive. I ran it: r"(\d+)\s+(?:tests?\s+)?(?:collected|passed)" matches 2 candidates in the first 100 lines — 2099 (from '2099 passed') and 2102 (from '2102 collected'). But test_count() at cdsfl_utils.py:91-108 parses 'N tests collected', i.e. the COLLECTION count. Comparing a pass count against a collection count mismatches by construction whenever anything is skipped: today the suite is 2549 passed + 7 skipped = 2556 collected. The check would emit STALE against a perfectly current document forever. Any repair must compare collected-to-collected, or match only the '(N collected)' form.

verdicts.title: cdsfl_onboard.py names a dead model and marks a retired route Required, contradicting check_model_keys.py
verdicts.reproduction:
Both outputs captured in the same tree. `python3 scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py --full < /dev/null` prints '!![MISSING] GEMINI_API_KEY (Required) / Gemini 3.1 Pro dispatch via Google GenAI API' and '!![MISSING] DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (Required) / DeepSeek Reasoner dispatch via DeepSeek API'. `python3 scripts/check_model_keys.py` prints '[PRESENT] GEMINI_API_KEY  (optional: legacy direct-Google fallback (panel uses OpenRouter since 2026-05-10))'. Source confirmed at scripts/check_model_keys.py:19-27 (REQUIRED = OPENROUTER, DEEPSEEK only) versus scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py:80-87.

Project record confirmed: .claude/CLAUDE.md:32 'Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview via OpenRouter API (google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview) — moved from direct Google API to OpenRouter on 2026-05-10'; :34 'DeepSeek V4 Pro via DeepSeek direct API (deepseek-v4-pro) — upgraded from R1-0528 on 2026-05-10; the older deepseek-reasoner is no longer listed by DeepSeek'. So the model name and the transport description in cdsfl_onboard.py are both stale, and the two scripts do contradict each other. Also verified the auditor's negative claim: `grep -rn WOLFRAM_API_KEY .env` returns only the line-12 archival comment, and the string appears in neither script.

One correction to the adjudication, which matters for the fix. GEMINI_API_KEY is not dead code: `grep -rn GEMINI_API_KEY --include="*.py"` shows eight live consumers under bench/, including bench/run_round_robin.py:2021-2023 (class GeminiReviewChat) and bench/decomposed_dispatch.py:398-400, which raise RuntimeError('GEMINI_API_KEY / GOOGLE_API_KEY not set') without it. What retired on 2026-05-10 was the PANEL route, not every consumer; GeminiReviewChat is referenced only from run_round_robin.py and not from bench/reference_runner_v2.py, so it is v1-era, but it still exists and still hard-fails. The proposed fix — delete onboard's dict and import REQUIRED/OPTIONAL from check_model_keys — would demote GEMINI_API_KEY to optional in the one surface that tells a new researcher what to obtain. Correct the descriptions and the DeepSeek model name; keep a note that direct-Google consumers remain in bench/, rather than silently reclassifying.

verdicts.title: cdsfl_onboard.py reports [FOUND] for the retired Wolfram MCP Bridge and does not check wolframscript
verdicts.reproduction:
`python3 scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py --full < /dev/null | grep -i wolfram` -> '  Wolfram MCP Bridge:' / '    [FOUND] Wolfram Local MCP Bridge', and separately '[FOUND] wolframalpha  Wolfram Alpha API client' under Optional packages.
  `ls -d /Applications/WolframLocalMCPBridge.app` -> present. scripts/cdsfl_onboard.py:261-271 tests only Path('/Applications/WolframLocalMCPBridge.app').exists(); there is no code path that can report anything but FOUND once the bundle exists.

verdicts.title: check_model_keys.py works exactly as specified
verdicts.reproduction:
`python3 scripts/check_model_keys.py; echo EXIT=$?` -> all five named keys [PRESENT], 'OK: all required model-route credentials present.', EXIT=0. Cross-checked against .env by name only: all nine entries non-empty; eight carry the `export ` prefix, SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY does not, and all nine parse under _env_file_names because scripts/check_model_keys.py:43-44 strips the prefix before partitioning. The `if val.strip()` guard at :47 means a declared-but-empty key reads as absent. WOLFRAM_API_KEY appears in neither REQUIRED nor OPTIONAL, consistent with its 2026-08-03 removal.

I ran my own leak scan rather than trusting the auditor's. I built 24 needle strings from the nine .env secrets (full value, first 8 chars, last 8 chars) and scanned the combined stdout+stderr of six invocations — check_model_keys.py, cdsfl_onboard.py --full, cdsfl_onboard.py --dry-run, cdsfl_seal_logs.py --verify, cdsfl_recover.py, cdsfl_qc.py. Result: 'leak: no' on every one; TOTAL LEAKS: 0. No key value is printed by any of the five scripts.

I also probed for the silent-failure shape the brief warns about and found none: with .env absent, _env_file_names returns an empty set and any required key falls through to MISSING and exit 1, so there is no path by which absence reports OK. The script says 'present', not 'valid' — it does not ping the endpoints — but it names itself a preflight and its output wording matches what it actually measures, which is the distinction the Wolfram-401 incident turned on. No defect found.

verdicts.title: None of the five audited scripts has test coverage
verdicts.reproduction:
grep -rln "cdsfl_qc\|cdsfl_utils\|cdsfl_onboard\|cdsfl_sv\|cdsfl_recover" bench/tests/ -> bench/tests/test_sv_commit.py only, and inspecting it (`grep -n` at lines 5 and 20) shows it imports `from cdsfl_sv import ...` and concerns cdsfl_sv.py alone.
  grep -rln "cdsfl_seal_logs" bench/tests/ -> no output.
  grep -rln "check_model_keys" bench/tests/ -> no output.
  python3 -m pytest bench/tests/ --co -q | tail -3 -> 2556 tests collected. python3 -m pytest bench/tests/test_verification_chain.py -q -> 98 passed. The gap is specific to scripts/, not general — the library beneath the broken seal verifier is well covered, which is precisely why the defect survived.

The ages are all independently verified above: F4 118 days (188-revision replay, two state changes), F1 107 days (single commit 2c966ca postdating the tuple return cb112c6), F3 105 days (crash reproduces from the file's first commit 991cde0). Routing this as NEEDS_RULING rather than a bug is the right call — it is a scope decision, not a defect. I would add one item to the proposed test file beyond the six listed: a test asserting that _verify_dir returns False for a chain whose underlying sealed FILE has changed, not only for a mutated sealed_chain.json, since that is the property the module docstring actually promises and the one the F1 fix does not deliver.

missed: SEAL VERIFICATION NEVER RE-READS THE SEALED FILES — scripts/cdsfl_seal_logs.py:141-155 with bench/verification_chain.py:727. This is the hole behind F1 and the auditor did not find it. verify_chain() performs zero file I/O: with builtins.open and pathlib.Path.read_text both replaced by a raiser, `VerificationChain.load_json('logs/chat/sealed_chain.json').verify_chain()` still returns (True, 'All 1 records verified.'). It has no reference to the log directory at all — load_json is handed only the seal path. Worse, every record is written with storage_mode='hash_only' (confirmed in logs/chat/sealed_chain.json), and bench/verification_chain.py:727 gates the payload_hash comparison on `if sealed_body['storage_mode'] == 'full_payload'`, so even the recorded hash is never re-checked. I recomputed the leaf by hand: logs/chat/README.md currently hashes to sha256:e4e19a99…f278ff, exactly matching the stored payload_hash; a one-byte addition yields sha256:990dfc2a…4126b. Nothing in the verify path performs that comparison. So --verify can only ever detect tampering with sealed_chain.json itself. The module docstring at scripts/cdsfl_seal_logs.py:16-18 promises 'any modification to a sealed file invalidates the Merkle root' and --help promises 'exit non-zero on tamper'; neither holds, and neither will hold after the F1 fix. Fixing only the tuple and declaring the seal layer repaired would re-light the green light over an open hole.

cdsfl_recover.py's HEADLINE SECTION IS STRUCTURALLY ONE COMMIT STALE AND ALWAYS CLAIMS A DIRTY TREE — scripts/cdsfl_recover.py:41-45. `python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py` prints docs/CURRENT_STATE.md verbatim as its first block, '## CURRENT STATE'. Right now that block says 'Last commit: `686c515`', 'Committed: 2026-08-04 04:09:35 +0100', 'Remote: diverged (ahead 97, behind 1)', 'Working tree: DIRTY — uncommitted changes present' and lists seven uncommitted files (.claude/CLAUDE.md, resources/RECOVERY.md, bench/tools/simulated_bench.py, and four others). Live state is HEAD 624b39a committed 2026-08-05 14:08:53, one uncommitted file, ahead 98. All seven listed files were committed BY 624b39a. Forty lines further down the same output, the script prints its own '## GIT STATE' block with the correct values — so one recovery output carries two contradictory git states, and the false one comes first. This is systematic, not a one-off: replaying the last eight revisions of docs/CURRENT_STATE.md, seven of eight record their own PARENT commit as 'Last commit' and all eight say 'Working tree: DIRTY', because cdsfl_sv.py regenerates the snapshot before making the commit it describes. qc cannot catch it — check_staleness inspects only ONBOARDING.md and RECOVERY.md. After a compaction this is the first thing an agent or the founder reads, and it names the wrong commit and invents seven phantom uncommitted files. That is the same shape as F5 but on the headline rather than a subsection, and 68 experiment directories is a less consequential lie than the wrong HEAD.

cdsfl_recover.py's PENDING WORK SECTION IS A PERMANENT SILENT NO-OP — scripts/cdsfl_recover.py:108-116. It calls read_section(RECOVERY.md, 'NEXT STEPS:', '\nARCHITECTURAL GAPS'). Neither literal exists in the file: `grep -c 'NEXT STEPS:' resources/RECOVERY.md` -> 0 and `grep -c 'ARCHITECTURAL GAPS' resources/RECOVERY.md` -> 0, and read_section returns '' when called directly. The script therefore prints '  (No pending work section found)' while resources/RECOVERY.md:2289 carries '**IMMEDIATE NEXT STEPS (consult HIL before proceeding):**' followed by eight numbered items (push local commits, wire OpenRouter tool-use, wire the DeepSeek specialist role, implement nu_k in O1, add Unpaywall/CORE/OpenAlex adapters, re-run the Exp 39-0 gate test, carry forward six lessons, promote specialist dispatch from shadow to live). I replayed all 194 revisions of RECOVERY.md: 'ARCHITECTURAL GAPS' vanished at f528314 (2026-04-09) and 'NEXT STEPS:' at f5e73ab (2026-04-14) and neither has returned. So `rs` has told every reader for 113 days that there is no pending work, over a live eight-item queue. Same class as F6 — a marker-matching check whose subject moved, failing to silence rather than to red.

THE PROPOSED F6 REGEX WOULD SHIP A PERMANENT FALSE POSITIVE. Measured, not inferred: r"(\d+)\s+(?:tests?\s+)?(?:collected|passed)" matches two candidates in RECOVERY.md's first 100 lines — 2099 (from '2099 passed') and 2102 (from '2102 collected') — while cdsfl_utils.test_count() at :91-108 parses 'N tests collected' and returns the COLLECTION count (2556 today). Comparing a pass count to a collection count mismatches by construction whenever anything is skipped; the suite is currently 2549 passed + 7 skipped = 2556 collected. Adopting the fix as written converts a silent no-op into a check that reports STALE against a correct document forever. Match only the '(N collected)' form, or normalise both sides.

THE F3 FIX RESTORES A CHECK THAT IS UNUSABLE AS-IS. Applying guard (2) alone — Path.exists wrapped so OSError returns False — lets check_broken_references complete, and it then emits 236 BROKEN_REF findings: 59 in experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md, 40 in resources/RECOVERY.md, 28 in the Consolidated Plan, 25 in resources/ONBOARDING.md. Sampled details include 'agenttools.wolfram.com/mcp', 'npx -y mcp-remote https://agenttools.wolfram.com/mcp' and 'bash bench/arc_sequencer.sh' — protocol-less URLs and shell commands that _is_likely_not_a_path does not filter. Neither proposed guard addresses this. Landing the crash fix without a heuristic pass replaces a loud failure with a report nobody can read, which in this project's own terms is a downgrade, not a repair.

report.resource: CDSFL human/agent-readable recovery document set — resources/ONBOARDING.md, resources/RECOVERY.md, resources/README.md, SHORTCUTS.md, MEMORY.md, MEMORY_EXCLUSIONS.md, OPENBRAIN_FINDING.md, docs/CURRENT_STATE.md, docs/GLOSSARY.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, REPRODUCING.md, MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md, the Desktop/repo tracker and consolidated-plan mirror pairs, experimental_notes/OUTSTANDING_QUEUE_to_BR2.md and Exp36_Ground_Truth_Reference_2026-04-08.md
report.spec_source:
Four specs govern this set, all quoted verbatim from the files themselves.

(1) resources/ONBOARDING.md:3-6 — "Last updated: 5 August 2026 14:08 BST" followed by "Read this document first if you are a new model instance, a new developer, or a reviewer picking up this project for the first time."

(2) resources/RECOVERY.md:5-6 — "How to rebuild full working context from the repository alone after a session loss, compaction event, or fresh start with a new model instance."

(3) resources/SHORTCUTS.md:13-17 — "The canonical and authoritative reference for metacognitive commands is `.claude/CLAUDE.md` (project-level directives) and `docs/REPRODUCING.md` § Metacognitive Commands. This document is a reader-facing summary; it must remain aligned with those files."

(2026-08-02
(2026-07-02/03

Mechanism, proven by execution:
$ python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py --dry-run 2>&1 | tail -40
...
Updated timestamp: /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/resources/ONBOARDING.md
Updated timestamp: /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/resources/RECOVERY.md
No experiment data — skipping ONBOARDING.md experiment update
Preserved manual content: /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/resources/RECOVERY.md

Source confirming the two paths are independent — scripts/cdsfl_sv.py:442-455 rewrites 'Last updated:' unconditionally with timestamp_now(); scripts/cdsfl_sv.py:196-199 returns False (preserving stale content) whenever _has_manual_content() finds >50 chars without the 'add manually after sv' placeholder.
findings.root_cause: update_timestamp() and update_onboarding_experiment() are separate, ungated code paths in scripts/cdsfl_sv.py. The timestamp write is unconditional; the content write is suppressed whenever the marker block holds manual prose — which it always does, because the block has been hand-written since April. Every sv run therefore advances the visible currency signal of ONBOARDING.md without touching a word of its body. RECOVERY.md escapes the same defect only because its 2026-08-05 correction block was written by hand today.
findings.consequence: ONBOARDING.md is the document that says 'Read this document first if you are a new model instance'. A model recovering from compaction reads a 5 August timestamp, treats the body as current, and is missing: the end-to-end pipeline proof (bench/tools/simulated_bench.py, 12/12 stages), the ALG-02-REF-01 planted-defect result, the routing-repair evidence, and — most damaging — the 5 August provenance correction and the standing SIM-A..E labelling rule that HEAD 624b39a exists entirely to record. An agent working from ONBOARDING alone could re-commit the exact provenance failure that was corrected today, because the document that greets it does not know the failure happened. This is the project's own named failure shape: a resource that looks fine and reports something false.
findings.proposed_fix: Two changes, both small. (a) In scripts/cdsfl_sv.py, gate update_timestamp() on the same condition as the content write: if _has_manual_content() suppressed the ONBOARDING block, either leave 'Last updated:' alone or rewrite it to 'Last updated: <date> (timestamp only — body last edited <git log -1 --format=%ad for the file>)'. A currency signal that can advance without the content advancing is not a currency signal. (b) Add the 3–5 August entries to the SV:LATEST_EXP block: the simulated bench, the provenance correction, and the SIM-A..E rule, mirroring what RECOVERY.md:98 already carries.
findings.effort: (a) ~15 lines in scripts/cdsfl_sv.py plus a regression test asserting the timestamp does not move when the body is preserved. (b) ~30 lines of prose lifted from RECOVERY.md:98-122 and the tracker.

findings.title: SHORTCUTS.md and docs/REPRODUCING.md both define `cy` as bare "Continue", dropping the standing live-experiment monitoring contract that .claude/CLAUDE.md carries

$ sed -n '200,245p' docs/REPRODUCING.md
| `cy` | Continue |

$ grep -nE '^\|\s*`?[a-z0-9]{1,4}`?\s*\|' .claude/CLAUDE.md
51:| `cy` | Continue the work AND apply live-experiment monitoring discipline: while any experiment/process runs, monitor ~every 60 s; on anything screwy/off, pause it, FFAFP (analyse with all tools), fix, then resume; always keep a terminal window open tailing the running experiment's full current output for the founder. (Standing directive 2026-05-18.) |

SHORTCUTS.md:13-17 names .claude/CLAUDE.md and docs/REPRODUCING.md as "canonical and authoritative" and states "it must remain aligned with those files" — so two of the three tables, including one of the two named canonical sources, carry the stale definition.

Persistent memory (MEMORY.md shorthand section) states the rule explicitly: "`cy` is no longer bare 'continue' — it carries this monitoring contract."
findings.root_cause: The 2026-05-18 standing directive was applied to .claude/CLAUDE.md and to the global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md but never propagated to the two repo-facing tables. There is no test or qc check asserting the three MC tables agree, so the divergence is invisible.
findings.consequence: `cy` is issued to authorise unattended overnight runs that cost real money on borrowed funds. An agent that learns `cy` from SHORTCUTS.md or REPRODUCING.md — the two documents a fresh instance is most likely to read, since SHORTCUTS.md is the reader-facing summary and REPRODUCING.md is the published reproducibility doc — will launch and walk away: no 60-second polling, no pause-and-FFAFP on anomaly, no terminal tail for the founder to inspect. The monitoring contract exists precisely because a run going wrong unobserved burns the budget. This is a silent capability regression, not a documentation nit.
findings.proposed_fix: Copy the .claude/CLAUDE.md:51 wording verbatim into resources/SHORTCUTS.md and docs/REPRODUCING.md § Metacognitive Commands. Then add a check to scripts/cdsfl_qc.py that parses the MC tables in all three files and fails on any command whose definition text diverges beyond whitespace — the three-way sync is asserted in prose (SHORTCUTS.md:13-17, resources/MEMORY.md 'Keep those two copies in sync on any change') and enforced nowhere.
findings.effort: Two edits plus ~30 lines of qc check.

'## Current State' spans lines 93 to 2424 — 2332 lines, 89% of the file — with no heading of any level inside it.

RECOVERY.md by contrast is well-structured for entry: newest first, with the 2026-08-05 provenance correction at line 98 above the 2026-08-04 'SESSION STATE … (READ THIS FIRST)' at line 123, and every older block explicitly marked '(superseded)'. Its weakness is the opposite one — the actual procedures sit at the end: '## Minimum Recovery (2 minutes)' at line 720, '## Standard Recovery (5 minutes)' at 2377, '## Full Recovery (10 minutes)' at 2386.

The first 40 lines of each are quoted in full under spec_source and F1/F7; both open with a title, a 'Last updated' line and a purpose statement, and RECOVERY.md then goes straight into the test-suite correction block rather than into a recovery procedure.
findings.root_cause: Append-only maintenance. Each session's entry is prepended inside the same '## Current State' heading, and no session has ever split it. RECOVERY.md avoided this by giving each session its own '## SESSION STATE — <date>' heading, which is why it remains navigable at almost the same file size.
findings.consequence: Honest assessment of the question asked: RECOVERY.md is still usable under compaction — newest-first ordering with dated headings means reading the first ~200 lines gets a reader genuinely current, and the ordering is correct today. ONBOARDING.md is not usable in the same way. There is no table of contents, no subheading to jump to, and no way to read 'just the current part' except by trusting that the top of a 2332-line block is the newest — which F1 shows it is not. In practice the recovery path has become 'read the tracker', and the tracker is in fact the best of the three: its resume pointer is dated 2026-08-05 14:20 BST at HEAD 624b39a and is accurate. That is a reasonable outcome, but it should be stated as the design rather than left as an accident, because ONBOARDING still tells readers to start with it.
findings.proposed_fix: Split '## Current State' into '### <date> — <headline>' subheadings, one per session entry, matching the convention RECOVERY.md already uses successfully; that alone makes the file greppable and gives a rendered table of contents. Then state the recovery order explicitly at the top of ONBOARDING: tracker first (it holds the resume pointer), then RECOVERY.md's newest blocks, then ONBOARDING for background. Two of those three already say something like this in scattered places; making it the first thing a recovering agent reads would match what actually works.
findings.effort: Mechanical heading insertion across ~40 entries, plus a short orientation paragraph.

findings.title: Three mechanisms in this document set work correctly and are worth recording as working

verdicts.title: ONBOARDING.md timestamped today, newest body content 2026-08-02; sv bumps date while skipping body
verdicts.reproduction:

$ grep -ci "simulated_bench|SIM-A|provenance correction|simulated panel" -> ONBOARDING 0, RECOVERY 5, tracker 4. Reproduced exactly.
$ python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py --dry-run 2>&1 | tail -50 -> 'Updated timestamp: .../ONBOARDING.md' ... 'No experiment data - skipping ONBOARDING.md experiment update'. Reproduced verbatim. (Confirmed non-destructive: mtime stayed Aug 5 14:08 and git status unchanged.)
STRONGER EVIDENCE THE AUDITOR DID NOT PRODUCE - the mechanism is visible in committed history, not just in a dry run:
$ git show 624b39a -- resources/ONBOARDING.md -> the entire diff is '-Last updated: 4 August 2026 04:00 BST / +Last updated: 5 August 2026 14:08 BST'. One line.
$ git show --stat --format='' <c> -- resources/ONBOARDING.md for 624b39a, 9396c43, 9cd8f62, 8690467 -> '1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)' on all four. The last commit that changed ONBOARDING's body is 91c6c7d (53 insertions, 2026-08-02).
So four consecutive sv commits advanced the currency signal and touched nothing else. In the same commit RECOVERY.md received 29 lines of real content, confirming the auditor's point that RECOVERY escaped only because it was hand-edited.
$ python3 -c "...import cdsfl_sv...; _has_manual_content(ONBOARDING) -> True; _has_manual_content(RECOVERY) -> True"
verdicts.correction:
Verdict stands, but two corrections to the reasoning and one to the fix.
(1) ROOT-CAUSE IMPRECISION. In the run the auditor exhibited, the suppressor that actually fired was `exp` being falsy - scripts/cdsfl_sv.py:761 `if exp:` ... :775 `else: print("No experiment data - skipping...")`. `_has_manual_content` was never consulted on that path. It is a second, independent suppressor and I verified it returns True, so both are live; but the printed line the auditor quoted as proof of the _has_manual_content path is proof of a different path. Right symptom, half the cause.
(2) THE PROPOSED FIX (a) IS WRONG AS WRITTEN. 'gate update_timestamp() on ... _has_manual_content()' would freeze 'Last updated:' permanently, because _has_manual_content is True on ONBOARDING today and has been since the block was hand-written in April. Commit 91c6c7d shows the body DOES get hand-edited sometimes; under that fix a genuine 2026-08-02 body update would have shipped with a stale April date. The auditor's own alternative - rewrite to 'Last updated: <date> (timestamp only; body last edited <git log -1 --format=%ad -- resources/ONBOARDING.md>)' - is the correct form and should be the one adopted. Deriving the body date from git is also strictly better than gating, because it cannot go stale.
(3) The claimed consequence is accurate: the SIM-A..E standing rule added to .claude/CLAUDE.md in 624b39a is absent from ONBOARDING's 'Standing Rules (Load-Bearing, Must Survive Compaction)' section (lines 25-36), which I read in full.

verdicts.correction:
Confirmed, with one qualification on item (1) that matters because the rest of the audit holds CURRENT_STATE.md up as the model to copy.
It binds its number to the WRONG commit. It reports 'HEAD `686c515`' and 'Remote: diverged (ahead 97, behind 1)', but $ git log --oneline -3 shows HEAD is 624b39a with 686c515 as HEAD~1, and $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py --dry-run reports 'ahead 98'. This is structural, not a one-off: sv generates CURRENT_STATE.md before creating the commit that ships it, so the file always names the commit preceding itself. For a document whose entire design argument is 'bind the number to a commit', the commit it binds to is never the commit it is published in. The '+ uncommitted working tree' qualifier keeps it honest rather than false, and the collection count is not sensitive to one commit, so this is LOW - but it should be fixed (amend the file post-commit, or record the tree hash instead) before the pattern is propagated to RECOVERY.md as F7 recommends.

missed: BLOCKING - scripts/cdsfl_qc.py CRASHES before completing, and five of this audit's proposed fixes depend on it. The `qc` metacognitive command is documented in resources/SHORTCUTS.md ('Quality control - run `scripts/cdsfl_qc.py` and fix reported issues') and in docs/REPRODUCING.md. $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_qc.py -> prints 'Checking timestamps... / Checking test consistency... / Checking experiment consistency... / Checking file references...' then dies with 'OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long' at scripts/cdsfl_utils.py:338 (`from_file.exists()`), called from scripts/cdsfl_qc.py:153 -> :337. $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_qc.py >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $? -> 1. ROOT CAUSE: check_file_references uses the regex `` `([^`]+/[^`]+)` `` to harvest backtick-quoted paths, which also captures any backtick-quoted PROSE containing a slash. $ python3 -c "re.finditer(...)" on experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md line 343 returns a 414-character span beginning ' to the consolidated plan (repo + Desktop mirror, byte-identical post-edit) immediately af...'; Path(...).exists() on a 414-byte component raises ENAMETOOLONG, and only the file READ at cdsfl_utils.py:310 is wrapped in try/except OSError - the .exists() calls are not. CONSEQUENCE, and this is the part that matters: check_broken_references is the FOURTH of seven checks (cdsfl_qc.py:327-347) and the findings report is printed only AFTER all seven (:348 onward), so the crash discards everything already computed. Running the six survivable checks in isolation shows what is being thrown away today (2 INFO from check_staleness, 1 INFO from check_glossary, 2 OK) - currently benign, but staleness and test-consistency are exactly the checks that would have flagged F1 and F7. AGE: the crashing text entered the tracker in commit 991cde0 (2026-04-22, `git log -S 'byte-identical post-edit'`), and check_file_references already existed at that revision - so the project's quality-control tool has been unable to finish a run for roughly 105 days. THIS INVALIDATES PART OF THE AUDIT'S REMEDY: F2, F3, F4, F9 and F11 all propose 'add a check to scripts/cdsfl_qc.py'. Any check appended to main() after line 337 will never execute. Repairing qc is a prerequisite for five of the fourteen findings, and the auditor ran the full documentation sweep without once invoking the tool the repo provides for exactly that sweep. Minimal fix: guard the .exists() calls with try/except OSError, and reject candidate refs longer than 255 bytes or containing whitespace before path resolution.
