findings.root_cause: There is no automated feed. Every Open Brain capture that exists was made by an operator (CC1) deciding, by hand, to call the CLI or MCP tool at some point during a session. The global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and resources/ONBOARDING.md both state that sv includes an Open Brain session summary, but the project-level /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/.claude/CLAUDE.md — which overrides the global — omits Open Brain entirely from the sv procedure, and scripts/cdsfl_sv.py implements that shorter contract faithfully. The script's own docstring scopes it to 'CURRENT_STATE.md, updates ONBOARDING.md, RECOVERY.md, and timestamps'. So the operator follows the project contract, the project contract does not mention Open Brain, and the store goes unfed. The March spike (84 writes) is when the operator was doing it manually and habitually; the collapse to 1-2 a month is that habit decaying with nothing structural underneath it.
findings.consequence: This is the founder's reported symptom, and it is fully explained. The last stored summary is 2026-08-02 because that is the last time an operator remembered. The substantial 08-04 and 08-05 sessions — which include the SIM-A..E provenance correction, a result the project treats as a first-order integrity event — exist only in git and in experimental_notes. After a compaction, RECOVERY.md step 13 instructs the agent to query Open Brain for session context; it will return a 2026-08-02 state and give no indication that three days of work are missing. A recovery resource that silently returns stale state is the exact failure shape this project names as most expensive.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a capture step to scripts/cdsfl_sv.py so that a successful --commit run also writes one session_summary. Roughly fifteen lines: after _commit_and_push succeeds, call open_brain.capture.capture_memory(text=<commit message>, source_agent='cc', memory_type='session_summary', area='verification', project='CDSFL'). Wrap it in try/except that prints a LOUD warning on failure but does not abort the commit — the commit is the more important artefact — and print an explicit success line naming the returned UUID, so a silent no-op is impossible to mistake for a write. Then reconcile the three sv specs: amend Constraint_Engineering/.claude/CLAUDE.md line 8 and the MC table at line 60 to name the Open Brain capture, so the project contract and the global contract agree. Note the dependency: the `project='CDSFL'` argument only exists on the standalone install, so OB-2 should be resolved first or the capture must omit it.
findings.effort: Small — about 15 lines in cdsfl_sv.py plus two documentation edits. Depends on OB-2 for the project argument.

Because the fork's capture.py has no concept of content_hash, signature or project, every write through the MCP path lands stripped of all three, and does so without any error. The 8 good rows were written when the operator used the CLI from a cwd where the editable package won.

First, tamper-evidence — the property this project documents as core and demonstrates in PAPER.md — is populated on 8 of 114 rows and has been silently off since 2026-06-08. Every new memory the founder's agents write is unverifiable, and nothing anywhere says so. Second, a future recovery is sent down a dead end in the direction opposite to the one assumed: an agent that reads Project_Genesis/open_brain/setup_db.sql will build a mental model with no content_hash, previous_hash, signature or idx_memories_project, none of which matches the live database. The stale fork is the decoy, not the standalone. This also corrects the audit brief's premise: OPENBRAIN_FINDING.md's statement that OpenBrain is 'a separate project at /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/OpenBrain/' is CORRECT, and the assumption that the working code is the Project_Genesis copy is what is wrong.

With PYTHONPATH gone, the pip-installed editable package wins from every cwd, the MCP gains the four missing tools and project scoping, and MCP writes start hash-chaining again. This is a one-hunk change to a config file and needs an MCP restart to take effect. Then remove or clearly tombstone /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Project_Genesis/open_brain/ so it cannot shadow the real package when an agent works from that cwd — a stub __init__.py that raises with the message 'moved to /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/OpenBrain; this fork is retired' is the loud option and is preferable to deletion. Verify afterwards by capturing one memory through the MCP and confirming content_hash is non-null.
findings.effort: Small for the .mcp.json edit (one hunk, plus MCP restart). Small-to-medium for retiring the fork, since Project_Genesis's own im_bridge.py imports from it and would need repointing.

First, DEFAULT_CONFIG at ob_bridge.py:51 resolves to the package's own tools/projects.json — the shipped example template, whose own _comment tells the reader to copy it to ~/.openbrain/projects.json — rather than to ~/.openbrain/projects.json where the real registry lives. The launchd plist passes no --config, so the template is what runs. Second, run_once treats a missing outbox directory as a normal, unremarkable condition and `continue`s without logging, so polling a literal '/path/to/your/project/ob_outbox' produces no output at all. The startup INFO line then prints the project name from that template, producing the sentence 'OB bridge watching projects: example (every 60s)' — which reads as a healthy daemon announcing its watch list, and is in fact the daemon announcing that it is watching nothing.
findings.consequence: Precisely the failure shape the founder asked me to hunt: a daemon that launchd reports as running with exit status 0, that logs a plausible startup line, that KeepAlive faithfully restarts, and that has ingested nothing for five months. The capability lost is CW's file-drop path — CW recorded on 2026-03-05 'OB bridge test: CW can now persist memories via file drop to ob_outbox/', and that capability has been dead since roughly 2026-03-09. Practical impact today is limited because CW has written nothing since March and the Project_Genesis outbox does not exist either, so no memories are actually being dropped and lost. The real cost is the false assurance: anyone checking whether something feeds Open Brain sees a live, healthy, purpose-named daemon and stops looking.
findings.proposed_fix: Two lines, in this order. (1) Point the daemon at the real registry: add <string>--config</string><string>/Users/georgejackson/.openbrain/projects.json</string> to ProgramArguments in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.openbrain.bridge.plist, then bootout and bootstrap the job. (2) Make the silent branch loud: in ob_bridge.py run_once, replace the bare `continue` with a log.warning naming the project and the missing path, rate-limited to once per project per process so it does not flood at 60-second cadence. Also change DEFAULT_CONFIG at line 51 to prefer ~/.openbrain/projects.json and fall back to the template only with a log.warning that the example config is in use — a daemon running on a file containing '/path/to/your/project' should say so at WARNING on every start. If the outbox path is genuinely dead infrastructure, the honest alternative is `launchctl bootout gui/$UID/com.openbrain.bridge` and removing the plist, so nothing claims to be feeding the store when nothing is.
findings.effort: Small — one plist edit plus a bootout/bootstrap, and about five lines in ob_bridge.py. Or a single bootout if the decision is to retire it.

findings.evidence:

The cleanest demonstration is my own diagnostic write. Before it, verify said 105 unhashed. Ninety seconds after writing one new row through the MCP:
$ python3 -m open_brain.cli verify
Hash chain verification: 114 memories
  Valid: 8
  Unhashed (pre-migration): 106
  Chain integrity: OK

A row created at 14:42:22 on 2026-08-05 is counted as pre-migration.

$ grep -n "pre-migration\|Chain integrity" /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/OpenBrain/open_brain/cli.py
422:    print(f"  Unhashed (pre-migration): {result['unhashed']}")
434:        print("  Chain integrity: OK")
findings.root_cause: The string 'pre-migration' at cli.py:422 is hardcoded and unconditional. It encodes an assumption that was true once — that any unhashed row must predate the hash-chain migration — and that assumption became false the moment a write path existed that produces unhashed rows. OB-2 created exactly that path. The verifier never compares a row's created_at against the migration boundary, so it cannot distinguish a legacy row from a live regression, and it reports both under a label that positively asserts the benign reading. 'Chain integrity: OK' at line 434 then evaluates only the 8 rows that have hashes; the 105 that do not are excluded from the check rather than counted against it, and the exit code is 0.
findings.consequence: This is the project's own catalogued failure shape running inside the tool whose entire job is to detect that shape. It sits alongside the verdict reader that matched 'NOT FALSIFIED' as 'FALSIFIED' and the netguard summary that printed 'Run with --netguard-strict' while strict was active. An operator running `verify` to check whether the memory store is trustworthy is told, in three affirmative lines, that it is — while 93% of it carries no integrity evidence at all and the number grows with every write. The label does more than fail to warn: it supplies a reassuring explanation for the number it is showing, which is worse than showing the number bare.
findings.proposed_fix: Two changes at cli.py:415-435. First, split the unhashed count by the migration boundary: compute max(created_at) over hashed rows and report 'Unhashed, pre-migration: N' and 'Unhashed, WRITTEN AFTER MIGRATION: M' as separate lines, so a live regression can never hide inside a legacy count. Second, make the verdict reflect coverage rather than only the hashed subset — print 'Chain integrity: OK (8 of 114 rows verifiable)' and, when M is greater than zero, print a warning line naming the newest unhashed row's date and exit non-zero. The rule the project already applies to Wolfram is the right one here: a check that did not verify a claim did not verify it, and must not read as though it did.
findings.effort: Small — about 20 lines in cli.py plus one extra query in the verify path, and a test asserting non-zero exit when a post-migration unhashed row exists.

findings.title: `session-context --project CDSFL` — the documented cure for cross-project contamination — silently returns a two-month-stale session summary as the latest
findings.evidence:
Unfiltered, the last summary is correct:
$ python3 -m open_brain.cli session-context --agent cc
Last session summary:
  CDSFL sv 2026-08-02 22:20 BST (second sv of the evening; small delta over 91c6c7d). HEAD 8690467, pushed...

With the project filter applied, it silently goes backwards by two months:
$ python3 -m open_brain.cli session-context --agent cc --project CDSFL
=== Session Context for CC ===

Pending tasks (0):
  (none)

Blocked tasks (0):
  (none)

Recent from other agents (0):
  (none)

Last session summary:
  CDSFL DIVERGENCE STUDY + PANEL (pr) COMPLETE 2026-06-03 (autonomous, founder asleep). VERDICT: 6/6 panel SOUND-WITH-CAVEATS...

No warning, no count of excluded rows, no indication that six newer CDSFL summaries were dropped.

The cause is that only 8 of 114 rows carry a project key at all:
$ psql -h localhost -U ob_reader -d open_brain -c "SELECT metadata->>'project' AS project, count(*), max(created_at)::date AS newest FROM memories WHERE metadata ? 'project' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;"
 CDSFL   | 7 | 2026-06-03
 cdsfl   | 1 | 2026-04-21
$ psql ... "SELECT metadata->>'source_agent', count(*) FROM memories WHERE NOT (metadata ? 'project') GROUP BY 1;"
 cc | 95
 cw |  2
 cx |  8

The filter is also case-sensitive:
$ python3 -m open_brain.cli list-recent --project CDSFL --limit 20 | grep -c "ID:"   -> 7
$ python3 -m open_brain.cli list-recent --project cdsfl --limit 20 | grep -c "ID:"   -> 1
findings.root_cause: The project filter is implemented as a plain metadata equality predicate with no handling for rows where the key is absent. Because OB-2 has stripped the project key from every write since 2026-06-08, 106 of 114 rows are invisible to it — including all six of the most recent CDSFL session summaries. The filter therefore does not select CDSFL material; it selects the eight rows that happened to be written through the standalone install between April and 2026-06-03. The 'last session summary' query returns the newest row that survives the filter, which is 2026-06-03, and presents it with the same wording and confidence as the true latest. The case split between 'CDSFL' and 'cdsfl' is a second, smaller instance of the same absence of normalisation.
findings.consequence: The remedy is worse than the disease. Unfiltered, the store gives a correct-but-cluttered answer: the true 2026-08-02 latest, mixed with March-era Genesis and CW material. Filtered, it gives a clean-looking, well-formatted, entirely wrong answer — a 2026-06-03 summary presented as current state, with 'Pending tasks (0)' and 'Blocked tasks (0)' reinforcing the impression of a tidy, complete picture. An agent recovering after compaction, following the sensible instinct to scope the query to its own project, is handed a two-month-old world model with nothing to signal the gap. If OB-1 is fixed and sv starts writing again without OB-2 being fixed first, this gets worse, not better: new writes will still lack the project key, so the filter's answer will keep receding from the truth while the store grows.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not enable the project filter in any recovery instruction until the backfill is done. Order matters. (1) Fix OB-2 so new writes carry project. (2) Backfill the 106 existing rows with a one-off UPDATE — ob_writer already holds UPDATE, no schema change needed — classifying by source: rows whose raw_text begins with 'CDSFL' or 'Session ' and originate from cc get project='CDSFL', cx and cw rows get project='project_genesis'. Normalise the existing 'cdsfl' row to 'CDSFL' in the same statement. This should be reviewed by the founder before running, since it is a judgement call on 106 rows. (3) Make the filter honest in the meantime: when a project filter is supplied, print the count of rows excluded for having no project key at all, e.g. 'Note: 106 rows carry no project tag and were not considered.' A filter that cannot see most of the store must say so. (4) Lowercase-normalise project on write and on query.
findings.effort: Medium. The CLI warning is small (about 10 lines). The backfill is a single UPDATE but needs founder review of the classification rule before it runs, and it is a write, so it was out of scope for this audit.

verdicts.correction:
Finding confirmed; the proposed fix has two problems I could demonstrate.

(1) TOMBSTONE CHOICE IS BACKWARDS. The fix prefers "a stub __init__.py that raises" over deletion. The global CLAUDE.md compaction protocol mandates `python3 -m open_brain.cli session-context --agent cc`, and I verified that command run from Project_Genesis cwd currently WORKS and returns the correct 2026-08-02 latest summary (the fork's read path is intact; only its write path is degraded). A raising stub converts a working, compulsory post-compaction recovery command into a hard failure whenever cwd is Project_Genesis. Renaming the directory (e.g. open_brain_retired/) achieves the same shadowing removal, is equally loud to a reader, and lets site-packages serve that command correctly. Prefer rename over raising stub.

(2) UNTESTED HAZARD IN THE SWITCH. Promoting the MCP to the standalone exposes four extra tools against a database that cannot serve them. The live DB has exactly one table:
$ psql ... "\dt" -> public.memories only
$ psql ... "SELECT to_regclass('public.epochs');" -> (empty)
$ python3 -m open_brain.cli list-epochs -> Error: relation "epochs" does not exist (rc=1)
$ python3 -m open_brain.cli verify-epochs -> same (rc=1)
Migrations 001/002/005 are applied (content_hash, previous_hash, signature, idx_memories_project all present) but 003_epochs.sql and 004_anchor_metadata.sql never were. record_anchor lives in epoch.py. $ wc -l logs/bridge_stderr.log -> 33 ; logs/ob_bridge.log identical, 34 lines, mtime Jun 10 16:59 — 56 days of polling, zero log output.
$ cat ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.openbrain.bridge.plist -> ProgramArguments contains no --config; KeepAlive true.

run_once (ob_bridge.py ~line 150): `if not outbox.is_dir(): continue` with no log call at any level — the silent branch is real.
Git history explains it: $ cd OpenBrain && git log --oneline -- tools/projects.json -> a9ff71c "Initial release" (2026-03-06), which introduced the file already as the placeholder template. The daemon was processing a project named "genesis" up to 2026-03-05 and has said "example" since 2026-03-09.
verdicts.correction:
Real, reproduced, and the false-healthy shape is genuine — but two things are wrong.

SEVERITY. BLOCKING is not supported by the auditor's own evidence, which concedes "Practical impact today is limited". Nothing is blocked and no memory is being lost: I confirmed the outbox the real registry names does not exist ($ ls /Users/.../Project_Genesis/ob_outbox/ -> No such file or directory), and CW has written nothing since 2026-03-05. The entire harm is false assurance to a reader checking what feeds the store. That is worth fixing; it is not BLOCKING alongside OB-1.

THE HEADLINE FIX DOES NOT WORK. Step (1) is "point the daemon at the real registry, ~/.openbrain/projects.json". I read that file:
$ cat ~/.openbrain/projects.json -> {"projects": {"project_genesis": {"root": "/Users/.../Project_Genesis", "outbox": "/Users/.../Project_Genesis/ob_outbox", "agents": ["cc","cx","cw"]}}}
That outbox directory does not exist, and run_once `continue`s on a missing outbox — process_outbox creates only the `processed/` subdirectory, and only after the outbox itself is confirmed to be a directory. So adding --config ~/.openbrain/projects.json changes the log line from "example" to "project_genesis" and ingests exactly as much as before: nothing. Applying step (1) alone would produce a daemon that looks MORE healthy while remaining just as dead — the same defect one layer up. Any real repair must also create the outbox (or drop it and take the auditor's own stated alternative: `launchctl bootout gui/$UID/com.openbrain.bridge`). Step (2), making the missing-outbox branch log at WARNING, is sound and is the part that actually matters.

verdicts.title: verify prints Chain integrity: OK and mislabels new rows pre-migration
verdicts.reproduction:
Reproduced verbatim, on today's data.

$ cd /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering && python3 -m open_brain.cli verify
Hash chain verification: 114 memories
  Valid: 8
  Unhashed (pre-migration): 106
  Chain integrity: OK

  Signatures: 8/8 verified
$ python3 -m open_brain.cli verify > /dev/null 2>&1; echo $? -> 0

The label is demonstrably false. The 106 includes a row created at 2026-08-05 14:42:22 (id d81755a9-...), i.e. minutes-old at audit time, counted as "pre-migration". Seven rows post-date the newest hashed row:
$ psql ... "SELECT created_at::date, left(raw_text,55) FROM memories WHERE content_hash IS NULL AND created_at > (SELECT max(created_at) FROM memories WHERE content_hash IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY created_at;"
-> 2026-06-08, 2026-06-09, 2026-06-11, 2026-07-03, 2026-08-02, 2026-08-02, 2026-08-05.

I verified the mechanism rather than assuming it. hashing.py verify_chain lines 75-81: `content_hash = mem.get("content_hash"); if not content_hash: result["unhashed"] += 1; continue` — unhashed rows are excluded from both broken_content and broken_chain, so they cannot influence the verdict. cli.py:422 prints the hardcoded "Unhashed (pre-migration): {n}"; cli.py:434 prints "Chain integrity: OK" whenever both broken lists are empty. The 8 hashed rows do form a genuine intact chain (genesis -> 1c1aa2a8 -> 53c384cc -> 9d97bc0e -> e1a01366 -> 0b6921b8 -> 4c6f0518 -> 35029d46 -> 36bafe9a), so "OK" is true of the 7% it examined and silent about the 93% it did not.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed as stated, including root cause. Two notes. (1) Severity: nothing is blocked — the harm is a false clean bill of health on the store's integrity tool, which is the project's own named failure shape, so it is not cosmetic, but it is a different kind of urgency from OB-1. (2) The proposed fix is sound and I found no way it breaks anything: splitting the unhashed count at the migration boundary and reporting coverage in the verdict line are both computable from data already in hand (max(created_at) over hashed rows). One addition worth folding in: exiting non-zero when M > 0 will make `verify` fail for the founder's current store on the very next run, which is the correct behaviour but should be expected rather than treated as a regression.

verdicts.title: session-context --project CDSFL silently returns a two-month-stale summary
verdicts.reproduction:
Reproduced exactly, side by side, in the same shell.

$ python3 -m open_brain.cli session-context --agent cc
... Last session summary:
  CDSFL sv 2026-08-02 22:20 BST (second sv of the evening; small delta over 91c6c7d). HEAD 8690467, pushed, in sync with origin, tree clean...

$ python3 -m open_brain.cli session-context --agent cc --project CDSFL
=== Session Context for CC ===
Pending tasks (0): (none)
Blocked tasks (0): (none)
Recent from other agents (0): (none)
Last session summary:
  CDSFL DIVERGENCE STUDY + PANEL (pr) COMPLETE 2026-06-03 ...

Two months backwards, no warning, no excluded-row count, and the three "(0)" lines actively reinforce a tidy-and-complete impression. (Unfiltered it correctly shows 1 blocked task and 7 rows from other agents.)

Data behind it:
$ psql ... "SELECT metadata->>'project', count(*), max(created_at)::date FROM memories WHERE metadata ? 'project' GROUP BY 1;"
 CDSFL | 7 | 2026-06-03
 cdsfl | 1 | 2026-04-21
$ python3 -m open_brain.cli list-recent --project CDSFL --limit 20 | grep -c "ID:" -> 7
$ python3 -m open_brain.cli list-recent --project cdsfl --limit 20 | grep -c "ID:" -> 1

Root cause verified in source, not inferred: OpenBrain/open_brain/db.py:327-329 —
    if project:
        proj_clause = " AND metadata->>'project' = %s"
A plain equality predicate reused across all five queries. Rows with the key absent are silently excluded (SQL NULL comparison), and the comparison is byte-exact, which is both the invisibility of 106 rows and the CDSFL/cdsfl split.
verdicts.correction:
Finding and root cause confirmed. The proposed fix's step (2) is measurably inadequate as specified. The stated backfill rule is "rows whose raw_text begins with 'CDSFL' or 'Session ' and originate from cc". I measured it:
$ psql ... "SELECT count(*) FROM memories WHERE NOT (metadata ? 'project') AND metadata->>'source_agent'='cc' AND (raw_text LIKE 'CDSFL%' OR raw_text LIKE 'Session %');" -> 32
$ ... AND NOT (...) -> 64
So the rule tags 32 of 96 untagged cc rows and leaves 64 behind, including unambiguously CDSFL material: "Authoritative CDSFL state as of 2026-04-17: HEAD cc6cc1a on branch exp...", "Exp 39 implementation phases 0-8 ALL COMPLETE on branch exp39-experime...", "Run 6 complete (wall-clock cap at 29,223s / 8h7m, 11 rounds, 299 findi...", "Gemini confer round 2 complete (PE 3-Gate + O1 Calibration Design)...". After running that backfill, `--project CDSFL` would still return a materially incomplete view while looking two-thirds more convincing. Any backfill needs a broader classifier (e.g. cc-sourced rows default to CDSFL, with cx/cw to project_genesis and a manual pass over the residue) — and step (3), the excluded-rows notice, should ship first and independently, since it is the part that makes the filter honest whatever the backfill does.

verdicts.title: OPENBRAIN_FINDING.md correct about location, stale about the filter
verdicts.reproduction:
Both halves check out.

Location claim is correct: resources/OPENBRAIN_FINDING.md:9-11 names /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/OpenBrain/, and $ python3 -m pip show open_brain reports "Editable project location: /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/OpenBrain". The directory exists with README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, WHITE_PAPER.md, pyproject.toml, migrations, launchd/, tools/.

Stale sentence confirmed. Lines 38-40 read "...cannot be cleanly separated without a per-project filter that does not currently exist on the public side." It does exist:
$ python3 -m open_brain.cli session-context --help
usage: open_brain session-context [-h] --agent {cc,cw,cx} [--project PROJECT]
  --project PROJECT   Scope context to a project
$ grep -n '"--project"' OpenBrain/open_brain/cli.py -> lines 40, 49, 57, 62, 75, 80 (capture, search, list-recent, pending-tasks, session-context, export)
and the standalone MCP capture_memory schema carries a 'project' property (verified by instantiating handle_list_tools, see OB-2).

Test count: $ cd OpenBrain && python3 -m pytest open_brain/tests/ -q --collect-only -p no:cacheprovider -> "440 tests collected". I did not run the full suite (it needs a live test database); collection matching 440 supports the auditor's figure.
verdicts.correction:
Confirmed, and the inversion correction is the right call — Project_Genesis/open_brain/ has mtimes of 2026-03-04 to 03-08 and no importers, while the pip-installed editable package is the OpenBrain directory.

One factual error in the audit's own summary line, which matters because the headline is what gets read. The headline says "2549 rows read" and "490 tests green". Neither is right: the live database contains exactly one table —
$ psql -h localhost -U ob_reader -d open_brain -c "\dt" -> public.memories only
$ psql ... "SELECT count(*) FROM memories;" -> 114
— and the standalone suite collects 440, not 490. 2549 is the CDSFL pytest count carried in commit 624b39a's message ("Suite 2549 passed / 7 skipped"), not an Open Brain row count. A summary that inflates a 114-row store to 2549 rows overstates exactly the health the audit is otherwise correctly qualifying.

On the fix: amending lines 38-40 and adding the canonical-vs-retired sentence are both right. The suggested RECOVERY.md:2398 cwd note should say more than "cwd matters" — after OB-2 is fixed it will no longer matter, so the note should be tied to the fork's removal rather than written as a permanent caveat.

missed: `verify-reasoning` reports an affirmative clean verdict on an empty set — the same failure shape as OB-4, in a different command, unreported. $ cd /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering && python3 -m open_brain.cli verify-reasoning cc prints: "Reasoning chain verification for cc: 0 checkpoints / Valid: 0 / Hash chain intact: True / Signatures: 0 valid, 0 invalid, 0 missing / Epoch proofs: 0 found, 0 missing / Anchored: 0 / Chain integrity: OK" and exits 0 (verified with output redirected, echo $? -> 0). README.md:195 advertises this as the command that "runs five checks: content hash integrity, hash chain continuity, signature validity, epoch inclusion, and epoch chain". All five ran against nothing and the tool answered "OK" and "intact: True". The store contains zero reasoning_checkpoint rows ($ python3 -m open_brain.cli reasoning cc -> "No reasoning checkpoints for agent 'cc'."), so the reasoning-verification surface has never had anything to verify. To be fair, the "0 checkpoints" count is printed — but an operator scanning for the verdict line reads OK, and rc=0 tells any script the same. This needs the identical treatment OB-4 proposes for `verify`: an empty verification set must not print an affirmative integrity verdict, and should not exit 0.

Migrations 003_epochs.sql and 004_anchor_metadata.sql were never applied to the live database, so the entire Merkle/anchor tier of the tamper-evidence story is inert on the founder's store — unreported, and a direct hazard to OB-2's own proposed fix. $ psql -h localhost -U ob_reader -d open_brain -c "\dt" returns only public.memories; $ psql ... "SELECT to_regclass('public.epochs');" returns empty; $ python3 -m open_brain.cli list-epochs and $ python3 -m open_brain.cli verify-epochs both fail with 'Error: relation "epochs" does not exist' (rc=1 on both, checked without a pipe so the code is python's, not tail's). Migrations 001/002/005 evidently were applied — content_hash, previous_hash, signature columns and idx_memories_project are all present in \d memories. ARCHITECTURE.md:239 lists "Epoch Merkle tree | BUILT | ... open_brain/migrations/003_epochs.sql, 38 tests" and README.md:248-251 documents seal-epoch/list-epochs/verify-epochs as available commands. The code is built and the tests pass; the schema it needs is absent from the store it is pointed at. Consequences: (a) per-row hash + Ed25519 signature is the only tamper-evidence the live store has, and $ python3 -m open_brain.cli prove <hashed-uuid> confirms it, printing "Merkle proof: none (epoch not sealed)" and "Anchor: none"; (b) OB-2's fix promotes the MCP to the standalone server, which exposes record_anchor (implemented in epoch.py) as a tool that will error on first use unless 003 and 004 are applied first. Mitigating detail: these commands fail loudly with a non-zero exit, so this is a deployment gap rather than a silent one — but it belonged in the audit, and it changes the safe ordering of OB-2's remediation.

`--project` is optional on every write surface with no default and no warning, which is the mechanism that will regenerate OB-5 after OB-5 is fixed. $ python3 -m open_brain.cli capture --help shows "[--project PROJECT]" as optional while --agent and --type are required; OpenBrain/open_brain/cli.py:40 declares it with no default and no required flag, and capture.py only adds the key `if project:`. The standalone MCP capture_memory schema likewise lists project among its properties without requiring it. So even after the .mcp.json fix and the backfill, every capture where the operator forgets the flag lands untagged and invisible to `--project CDSFL` — the same habit-decay failure OB-1 correctly diagnoses for sv, one layer down. OB-5's fix (4) proposes lowercase normalisation but nothing that makes the tag happen by default. The durable repair is a per-install default project (config or environment) applied at capture time, so untagged writes become impossible rather than merely discouraged.

findings.title: cdsfl_recover.py --full prints two git states in one run and they disagree; the stale one is structurally guaranteed to be exactly one commit behind, every time
findings.evidence:
$ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py --full
## CURRENT STATE
- **Last commit:** `686c515` TTS + plain-English record: the pipeline proven end to end
- **Committed:** 2026-08-04 04:09:35 +0100
- **Remote:** diverged (ahead 97, behind 1)
- **Working tree:** DIRTY — uncommitted changes present
Uncommitted files:
- `M .claude/CLAUDE.md`
- `M bench/tools/simulated_bench.py`
- `M resources/RECOVERY.md`  [+4 more]
...
## GIT STATE
  Last commit: 624b39a sv: PROVENANCE CORRECTION...
  Committed: 2026-08-05 14:08:53 +0100
  Remote: diverged (ahead 98, behind 1)
  Uncommitted:
    M experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md

Mechanism proven: $ git show --name-only --format="" 624b39a  →  .claude/CLAUDE.md, bench/logs/simulated_bench_last.json, bench/tools/simulated_bench.py, docs/CURRENT_STATE.md, experimental_notes/OUTSTANDING_QUEUE_to_BR2.md, experimental_notes/Simulated_Bench_First_Full_Run_2026-08-04.md, experimental_notes/adversarial_records/simulated_panel_alg02_findings_2026-08-04.json, resources/ONBOARDING.md, resources/RECOVERY.md — i.e. CURRENT_STATE.md's entire "Uncommitted files" list is the set of files that WERE committed in HEAD. Its header reads "Generated: 5 August 2026 14:08 BST", byte-identical to HEAD's commit timestamp (git show -s --format='%h %ci' HEAD → 624b39a 2026-08-05 14:08:53 +0100).
findings.root_cause: scripts/cdsfl_sv.py calls git_state() at line 724 and writes docs/CURRENT_STATE.md at line 747, then commits at the end of main(). The snapshot is therefore always taken pre-commit: it records the parent commit as "Last commit" and records the about-to-be-committed files as "uncommitted". cdsfl_recover.py:45 then prints that file verbatim as its first and largest section, above its own live GIT STATE section.
findings.consequence: The first thing a recovering agent reads after the section header "## CURRENT STATE" is a wrong commit hash carrying a fresh-looking timestamp, and a DIRTY working-tree list naming seven files that are in fact committed and clean. An agent acting on it may try to re-commit already-committed work, or conclude the previous session ended mid-edit. Because the correct GIT STATE section appears ~40 lines later in a visually identical format, the reader has no cue which to believe — and the wrong one is first and better formatted.
findings.proposed_fix: In cdsfl_sv.py, re-generate docs/CURRENT_STATE.md immediately AFTER the commit succeeds (amend, or write-then-commit-again), or have it record the commit it is about to create. Failing that, stamp CURRENT_STATE.md with an explicit "state as of PRE-COMMIT, parent = <hash>" banner, and in cdsfl_recover.py print the live GIT STATE section FIRST and label the CURRENT_STATE block "snapshot from last sv (pre-commit)".
findings.effort: small

findings.title: The recovery script's PENDING WORK section has printed "(No pending work section found)" for 113 days because it searches for two markers that were deleted from RECOVERY.md in April

  (No pending work section found)

Code: pending = read_section(recovery, "NEXT STEPS:", "\nARCHITECTURAL GAPS")

$ python3 -c "..."
literal "NEXT STEPS:" present: False
literal "NEXT STEPS" present: True
literal "ARCHITECTURAL GAPS" present: False

  ctx: '**IMMEDIATE NEXT STEPS (consult HIL before proceeding):**'

$ git log --format='%h %ci %s' -S "NEXT STEPS:" -- resources/RECOVERY.md | head -1
f5e73ab 2026-04-14 07:21:18 +0100 sv: Exp 39-0 gate complete...
$ git show f5e73ab:resources/RECOVERY.md | grep -c "NEXT STEPS:"   → 0
$ git show f5e73ab^:resources/RECOVERY.md | grep -c "NEXT STEPS:" → 1
(113 days from 2026-04-14 to 2026-08-05)

Meanwhile the writer uses different markers:
$ grep -n "SV:PENDING" scripts/cdsfl_sv.py resources/RECOVERY.md
scripts/cdsfl_sv.py:233:_RECOVERY_MARKER_START = "<!-- SV:PENDING_START -->"
scripts/cdsfl_sv.py:234:_RECOVERY_MARKER_END = "<!-- SV:PENDING_END -->"

resources/RECOVERY.md:2375:<!-- SV:PENDING_END -->
findings.root_cause: The writer (cdsfl_sv.py) maintains the pending-work block between HTML comment markers SV:PENDING_START/END; the reader (cdsfl_recover.py:111) looks for the plain-text markers "NEXT STEPS:" and "ARCHITECTURAL GAPS", which the writer never emits and which were removed from RECOVERY.md at f5e73ab (2026-04-14) and f528314 (2026-04-09) respectively. read_section returns "" on a missing start marker with no error, and the caller's else-branch prints a message indistinguishable from "there genuinely is no pending work".
findings.consequence: This is the single item a recovering agent most needs — what to do next — and the documented recovery command reports it as empty, with exit code 0, while 1576 lines of live pending work sit between the SV:PENDING markers in the same file the script just opened. An agent that trusts the output concludes there is no outstanding work and either idles, asks the founder to re-specify from scratch, or picks its own next task. This is the exact failure shape the project catalogues: not an error, a confident empty answer.
findings.proposed_fix: Change cdsfl_recover.py:111 to read between the markers the writer actually emits: read_section(recovery, "<!-- SV:PENDING_START -->", "<!-- SV:PENDING_END -->"). Additionally make read_section's miss loud: when a start marker is absent, print "MARKER NOT FOUND in <path>: '<marker>' — section skipped" rather than a message that reads as a valid empty result. A test asserting that PENDING WORK is non-empty against the real RECOVERY.md would have caught this on day one.

findings.title: The recovery script reports "(No experiment logs found)" while 58 experiment directories exist, because one halted run at the highest number blanks the section permanently
findings.evidence:

## LATEST EXPERIMENT

  (No experiment logs found)

$ ls bench/logs/ | wc -l   → 315
$ ls -d bench/logs/exp* | wc -l   → 109

$ python3 -c "...latest_experiment()..."
exp dirs matched: 58
max exp number found: 53
candidates for max: ['exp53_control_zero_live_20260729T222431Z', 'exp53_control_zero_live_20260801T005649Z']
  exp53_control_zero_live_20260729T222431Z -> exp*_report.json: [] | all json: ['checkpoint.json', 'macrophage_shadow_r00.json', ...]
  exp53_control_zero_live_20260801T005649Z -> exp*_report.json: [] | all json: ['checkpoint.json', ...]
latest_experiment() -> None

$ for d in exp49_... exp48_... exp46_...; do echo "$d -> $(ls bench/logs/$d/exp*_report.json | wc -l) report json"; done
exp49_engineering_exam_live_20260729T062320Z -> 1 report json
exp48_chemistry_exam_live_20260729T044134Z -> 1 report json
exp46_stage6_locationkey_live_20260728T103151Z -> 1 report json
findings.root_cause: latest_experiment() (cdsfl_utils.py:133-140) computes max_n over all exp<N> directories, then iterates ONLY over candidates whose number == max_n, `continue`-ing past any that lack an exp*_report.json, and falls through to `return None`. It never backs off to N-1. Exp 53 is the deliberately halted zero-plant control (halted R3/16, per the tracker), so it wrote checkpoints but no report — and by being the highest number it permanently hides Exp 49, the most recent experiment that actually completed.
findings.consequence: A recovering agent is told, in the project's own recovery command, that the project has run no experiments. The failure mode is monotone and permanent: every future halted or aborted run at a new high-water number re-blanks the section for all subsequent recoveries. It also silently propagates into cdsfl_sv.py, which calls the same function at line 732 and prints "none found", then writes "Experiments 12–? ALL COMPLETE" with status UNKNOWN into RECOVERY.md's pending block (cdsfl_sv.py:247-251).
findings.proposed_fix: Make the loop descend: iterate experiment numbers from max_n downward, and within each number iterate candidates by mtime, returning the first directory that has a parsable report. Separately, when the highest-numbered directory has no report, say so explicitly — "Exp 53 (2 dirs) present but no report.json; showing Exp 49 as latest complete" — because a halted top-numbered run is itself state a recovering agent needs.
findings.effort: small

verdicts.title: cdsfl_recover.py --full prints two disagreeing git states; CURRENT_STATE.md is a pre-commit snapshot
verdicts.reproduction: $ python3 scripts/cdsfl_recover.py --full — '## CURRENT STATE' block reports Last commit `686c515`, Committed 2026-08-04 04:09:35, 'Working tree: DIRTY' with 7 files; '## GIT STATE' 40 lines later reports 624b39a, 2026-08-05 14:08:53, DIRTY with 1 file. $ git show -s --format='%h %ci' HEAD → 624b39a 2026-08-05 14:08:53 +0100; HEAD~1 → 686c515 2026-08-04 04:09:35. $ git show --name-only --format='' 624b39a returns 9 files; the 7 named as 'uncommitted' in CURRENT_STATE.md are exactly 7 of those 9 (the other two, docs/CURRENT_STATE.md and resources/ONBOARDING.md, are the ones sv modifies after the snapshot). Ordering confirmed in source: sed -n '700,830p' scripts/cdsfl_sv.py — git_state() at 724, state_path.write_text at 747, _commit_and_push at 805. No pre-commit banner exists in generate_current_state (scripts/cdsfl_sv.py:358-408). cdsfl_recover.py:45 prints the file verbatim as its first section; its own live GIT STATE is at :61-71.
verdicts.correction: Finding stands. Two qualifications on the write-up. (a) 'exactly one commit behind, every time' is the best case, not a guarantee — it holds when sv --commit is the last commit; if further commits land after an sv, or sv is run without --commit and the founder commits separately, the drift is larger. The invariant that actually holds is 'always at least one commit stale, always by construction'. (b) The first proposed fix is subtly broken: regenerating CURRENT_STATE.md after the commit and using `git commit --amend` changes the hash again, so the file would then name the pre-amend hash — the same self-reference error in a new place. Write-then-commit-again produces a second commit whose snapshot names the first, i.e. still one behind. Only the banner option ('state as of PRE-COMMIT, parent = <hash>') plus printing GIT STATE first is sound.

verdicts.reproduction: All five sources queried in one pass on this machine: git log → 624b39a; open_brain.cli session-context → 8690467; cdsfl_recover.py '## CURRENT STATE' → 686c515; cdsfl_recover.py '## GIT STATE' → 624b39a; tracker line 12 → 624b39a. Tree state: OB 'tree clean'; git status 'modified: experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md'; CURRENT STATE 'DIRTY' with 7 files; GIT STATE 'DIRTY' with 1 file; tracker line 12 'tree clean'. Remote: git status 'up to date with origin/exp39-experimental'; recover.py 'diverged (ahead 98, behind 1)' in both sections; tracker 'in sync with origin/exp39-experimental (0/0)'. I independently verified the tracker's nothing-running claim: `ps aux | grep -E 'reference_runner|launch_exp|detached_launch|simulated_bench' | grep -v grep | wc -l` → 0, and `ps aux | grep -c '[M]acOS/wolfram -run'` → 0. I also verified the no-test-coverage root cause: `grep -rln 'cdsfl_recover|cdsfl_utils|cdsfl_sv' . --include='*.py'` returns only the scripts themselves plus bench/tests/test_sv_commit.py, whose 28 tests all target staging and commit-message path validation — nothing asserts on recover.py output, latest_experiment, read_section, or the remote comparison.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed as a roll-up, with one internal inconsistency that should not survive into a fix. The headline claims 'the only source that is correct is the hand-maintained Desktop tracker', but F13's own evidence shows the tracker asserting 'tree clean' while the tree is dirty — and dirty specifically because of the tracker mirror the pointer update produced. The tracker is correct on HEAD, remote and what is running, and wrong on tree state, for a structural reason identical to F1: it records the state that existed just before its own edit. That makes the manual path stale-by-construction too, not merely the automated one, and it strengthens rather than weakens the case for the F12 fix that binds the pointer advance and the commit into one operation. The two proposed changes are correct; the regression test should assert on tree state as well as the two git sections.

missed: scripts/cdsfl_qc.py — the founder's documented `qc` command CRASHES and has never reported a finding in 105 days. This is the project's own staleness detector, and it is the single most on-theme defect in the resource. `python3 scripts/cdsfl_qc.py` → prints 'Checking timestamps... / Checking test consistency... / Checking experiment consistency... / Checking file references...' then dies with an unhandled `OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long` raised at scripts/cdsfl_utils.py:338 inside check_file_references, called from cdsfl_qc.py:153 via check_broken_references at cdsfl_qc.py:337; exit code 1. Because main() accumulates into all_findings and prints the FINDINGS report only at the end (cdsfl_qc.py:348-370), NOTHING is ever reported, and three further checks (glossary, onboard-script wiring, log seals) never run at all. Root cause: the reference regex at cdsfl_utils.py:318, r"`([^`]+/[^`]+)`", matches the prose spanning BETWEEN two unrelated inline-code spans on one line; on this repo it produces candidate 'paths' of 234-533 characters, and Path(...).exists() on a single component over 255 bytes raises OSError, which the surrounding code does not catch. The file that kills it is the mandated first-read tracker itself: I isolated it by iterating every *.md under the repo, and the first crash is experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md. I bisected all 54 commits that touched that file by replaying the exact matching logic against each `git show <sha>:experimental_notes/CDSFL_Agent_Operational_Plan.md` — EVERY one crashes, from 991cde0 (2026-04-22, the commit that introduced the file) to 9396c43 (2026-08-04). qc has therefore been dead since the day the tracker was created, 105 days. The loss is material, not theoretical: running check_file_references directly, resources/RECOVERY.md yields 40 broken references including line 730 `~/.claude/plans/agile-wondering-hejlsberg.md` — the exact missing file the auditor found by hand in F9 item 6 — and resources/ONBOARDING.md yields 25. The tool that would have caught F9 and F15 automatically has been silently producing zero output since April, and the project CLAUDE.md:11, project CLAUDE.md:61, SHORTCUTS.md:40 and SHORTCUTS.md:65 (`rs qc`) all still instruct an agent to run it and 'fix reported issues'. Fix: wrap the exists() calls at cdsfl_utils.py:335-347 in try/except OSError, and bound the regex — reject candidates over ~255 bytes or containing whitespace runs — so a prose span between two code spans is never treated as a path.

resources/RECOVERY.md:2400 — the documented Full Recovery step 14 command cannot run as written from the repository it documents. `python3 cw_handoff/im_service.py read` executed from /Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering returns "can't open file '.../Constraint_Engineering/cw_handoff/im_service.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory", exit 2. The path is relative to Project_Genesis and RECOVERY.md never says to change directory (the global CLAUDE.md:238 `r` definition does). F8 treats this site as a source of silent stale data; it is in fact a broken command. Either way it should go in the same sweep.

docs/CURRENT_STATE.md is committed at HEAD carrying the F3 failure. `git show HEAD:docs/CURRENT_STATE.md | grep -A3 'Latest Experiment'` returns 'No experiment logs found.' The finding was reported only against cdsfl_recover.py's live output, but the same false claim is in version control and reaches any fresh clone, any reader of the KEY FILES list ('docs/CURRENT_STATE.md — Machine-generated state snapshot'), and the first section cdsfl_recover.py prints. The same committed file also carries the F5 wrong remote figure ('Remote: diverged (ahead 97, behind 1)') and the F1 wrong HEAD. Fixing the two utils functions repairs the script; the committed snapshot stays wrong until the next sv regenerates it.

The SV:PENDING block that F2's proposed fix would read is itself 63 days stale, so the fix as written converts a confident empty answer into a confident wrong one. Extracting the block between resources/RECOVERY.md:799 and :2375, its section headings in file order are '2026-06-03, post-divergence-study', '2026-06-02 → 03', '22–23 May 2026', '20 April – 17 May 2026'. The first 30 lines cdsfl_recover.py:113 would print begin '## Current Pending Work (2026-06-03, post-divergence-study) — DECISION: AUTONOMOUS BUILD MODE', a block whose resume instruction is that Exp 42 relaunches after the layer-2 fix; Exp 42 through 49 and 53 have since run. The block is never refreshed automatically — `python3 scripts/cdsfl_sv.py --dry-run` prints 'Preserved manual content: resources/RECOVERY.md' because _has_manual_content (cdsfl_sv.py:165-178) finds no placeholder in 125,435 characters. Any repair to the PENDING WORK section must either point at a maintained source (the tracker's ★ RESUME POINTER, or experimental_notes/OUTSTANDING_QUEUE_to_BR2.md, mtime today) or print the section's own date so staleness is visible.
